title: Self-hostable sync server: OSS release packaging
description:
## Goal
Package the sync server as a clean OSS release so users can self-host instead of using hosted sync. Hosted sync remains included with the license; this is the open-source path.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 10 — explicitly deferred per PRD §26 (tension: cloud-first vs self-host).

## Scope
- Extract sync server to a standalone repo (or workspace) with permissive OSS license
- Dockerfile + docker-compose for one-command self-host
- Configuration docs (DB, secrets, OAuth callback URLs, Telegram webhook, magic-link email provider)
- Migration tooling
- Desktop client config: point at custom sync server URL
- Release pipeline: tagged releases, checksums

## Out of scope
- Migrating users between hosted and self-host (manual export/import is enough at MVP)

## Done when
A new operator can clone the OSS sync repo, run `docker compose up`, point a fresh desktop client at it, sign in via magic link, and complete a capture-to-review loop.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §20 Architecture, §22 Risks (cloud-first vs self-host), §26 Tensions Carried Forward.

title: OSS-01: Extract sync server as OSS-ready package (LICENSE, README, CONTRIBUTING, COC, SECURITY)
description:
## Goal
Extract the sync server into a clean, OSS-ready package — license, README, CONTRIBUTING, code of conduct — so external operators can self-host without inheriting any of the desktop / Telegram-bot / hosted-only assumptions.

## Scope
- Confirm `server/` workspace is a self-contained, importable-on-its-own deployable; remove or guard any internal-only dependencies (private utilities, hosted-only env vars)
- Add `server/LICENSE` (Apache-2.0 or MIT — pick one explicitly; document why in CONTRIBUTING)
- Add `server/README.md`: project description, what it does, what it doesn't do, quickstart link to docker-compose, links to config docs
- Add `server/CONTRIBUTING.md`: dev setup, test commands, PR process, issue triage labels
- Add `server/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (Contributor Covenant 2.1 standard)
- Add `server/SECURITY.md` (private security disclosure email + response SLA)
- `server/package.json` `name` becomes a publishable name (e.g., `calmly-sync-server`); set `repository`, `homepage`, `bugs`
- Strip references to the hosted-only telemetry/crash endpoints — those endpoints should still exist but be optional / disable-by-default in self-host
- Add a `SELF_HOSTING.md` index pointing to the dedicated docs (built in `oss_config_docs`)

## Files
- `server/LICENSE`
- `server/README.md`
- `server/CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `server/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`
- `server/SECURITY.md`
- `server/SELF_HOSTING.md` (skeleton — fleshed out in `oss_config_docs`)
- `server/package.json` (metadata fields)

## Acceptance
- A reviewer can clone only `server/` (no other workspace) and read README + CONTRIBUTING and understand how to start
- License is unambiguously chosen and present
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/server build` still passes after metadata + dependency cleanup
- No internal-only env var is required to start the server in OSS mode (verify by booting with the documented minimum env set)

## Notes
- This task does NOT split the repo into a separate Git repo; it makes the workspace OSS-ready in place. Repo split is a logistics step at release time.
- Dockerfile + compose is the next task (`oss_dockerfile_compose`).

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging ("Optional self-hostable sync server — published as open source"), §20 Architecture (optional self-host build), §22 (cloud-first vs self-host risk), §26 (tension carried forward), §23 step 10.

title: OSS-02: Dockerfile + docker-compose for one-command self-host (Postgres included)
description:
## Goal
Ship a production-grade `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` so a new operator can run `docker compose up` and have a working sync server (with Postgres) reachable on a known port.

## Scope
- Multi-stage `server/Dockerfile`:
  - Stage 1: build with pnpm + node 20; install deps, run `pnpm --filter @calmly/server build`
  - Stage 2: minimal `node:20-slim` runtime; copy build output + production node_modules; runs as non-root user `node`
  - Healthcheck pinging `/health`
  - Image labels: `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `version`, `licenses`
- `deploy/docker-compose.yml` (separate from the dev compose at repo root):
  - `sync` service built from `server/Dockerfile`
  - `postgres:16` service with named volume `calmly_pg_data`
  - Healthcheck-aware `depends_on` so `sync` waits for Postgres
  - Env-driven config via `.env` (template `deploy/.env.example`)
  - Default ports: sync `:3001`, Postgres internal-only
  - Migration job runs once on startup (entrypoint or separate one-shot service)
- `deploy/README.md`: quickstart (clone, copy `.env.example`, generate secrets, `docker compose up`)

## Files
- `server/Dockerfile`
- `server/.dockerignore`
- `deploy/docker-compose.yml`
- `deploy/.env.example`
- `deploy/README.md`

## Acceptance
- `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d` results in a healthy sync server reachable at `http://localhost:3001/health`
- Migrations run automatically on first up; subsequent `up` is idempotent (no re-running of completed migrations)
- Container runs as non-root; image size is reasonable (target < 300 MB)
- Stopping and restarting preserves data via the named Postgres volume
- Image builds on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64

## Notes
- Configuration docs (env var reference, OAuth callback URLs, Telegram webhook, magic-link email) are written in `oss_config_docs`.
- Migration tooling polish (rollback notes, backups) is `oss_migrations_polish`.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging (self-hostable), §20 Architecture (optional self-host build), §23 step 10.

title: OSS-03: Self-hosting configuration docs (env vars, OAuth callbacks, Telegram webhook, email)
description:
## Goal
Write the configuration documentation an operator needs to take a self-hosted sync server from "container running" to "fully wired with auth, calendars, and Telegram" — covering every required env var, every external callback URL, and every secret-generation step.

## Scope
- Document every env var consumed by the server, grouped by domain:
  - Core: `DATABASE_URL`, `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `NODE_ENV`
  - Secrets: `SESSION_SECRET`, `MAGIC_LINK_SIGNING_SECRET` (with `openssl rand -base64 32` snippets)
  - Auth: `BASE_URL` (used to construct callback URLs)
  - Email: `EMAIL_PROVIDER` (resend|console|smtp), `RESEND_API_KEY`, SMTP fields if relevant, `EMAIL_FROM`
  - Calendar OAuth: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MS_CLIENT_ID`, `MS_CLIENT_SECRET`, callback paths
  - Telegram: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, webhook URL (`{BASE_URL}/telegram/webhook`)
- For each external service, exact step-by-step setup:
  - Google Cloud Console: create OAuth client, add redirect URI `{BASE_URL}/auth/google/callback`, scopes
  - Microsoft Entra ID: app registration, redirect URI, delegated permissions for Calendar.Read
  - Resend: API key, verified sender domain
  - Telegram BotFather: create bot, get token, set webhook command
- TLS / reverse proxy guidance: a brief section on running behind nginx / Caddy / Traefik with HTTPS (required for OAuth callbacks)
- Desktop client config: how to point a client at a custom server URL (cross-references `oss_desktop_custom_server`)
- Troubleshooting section: common boot failures (bad DATABASE_URL, missing secrets, callback URL mismatch)

## Files
- `server/SELF_HOSTING.md` (full guide — was a skeleton from `oss_extract_package`)
- `server/docs/env-reference.md` (table of every env var: name, required?, default, description)
- `server/docs/oauth-google.md`
- `server/docs/oauth-microsoft.md`
- `server/docs/email-magic-link.md`
- `server/docs/telegram-webhook.md`
- `server/docs/reverse-proxy.md`

## Acceptance
- Env-reference table matches the actual config schema in `server/src/config.ts` exactly (verified by a generation/check script)
- A first-time operator following SELF_HOSTING.md end-to-end reaches a working sync + magic-link auth + at least one calendar OAuth flow
- Every callback URL is shown with a `BASE_URL` placeholder so copy-paste works after substitution
- Secret-generation snippets work on macOS, Linux, and Windows (PowerShell variant)

## Notes
- Documentation is OSS surface; keep tone neutral and operator-focused, not marketing-y.
- Don't document hosted-only secrets / endpoints in this self-host guide.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §20 Architecture, §15 Calendar Integration (Google + Microsoft 365), §23 step 10.

title: OSS-04: Migration tooling polish — idempotency, rollback notes, backup procedure
description:
## Goal
Polish the database migration tooling for self-hosters — idempotent migrations, documented rollback, and clear backup recommendations — so operators can upgrade Calmly versions without data loss.

## Scope
- Audit all existing migrations under `server/migrations/` for idempotency: every migration must be safely re-runnable (use `IF NOT EXISTS`, guarded `DO $$ BEGIN ... EXCEPTION ...`, etc., or rely on the migration runner's tracking table)
- Verify the migration runner records every applied migration in a tracking table and refuses to re-apply a completed one
- Add a migration template + brief authoring guide: forward-only style, no destructive statements without a documented rollback path, additive changes preferred
- Rollback notes: for each existing migration, document in a comment whether/how to reverse it; ship a `MIGRATIONS.md` summarizing
- Backup recommendations: documented procedure using `pg_dump` for self-hosters; suggested cadence; restore drill
- `bin/calmly-server migrate up` and `bin/calmly-server migrate status` CLI subcommands (status shows applied + pending)
- Pre-flight: server refuses to start if pending migrations exist AND `AUTO_MIGRATE=false` (operator opt-in to auto-apply)

## Files
- Audit + minor edits across `server/migrations/*.sql`
- `server/migrations/_template.sql.tmpl`
- `server/MIGRATIONS.md` (authoring guide + per-migration rollback notes)
- `server/docs/backups.md` (pg_dump procedure, restore drill)
- `server/src/cli/migrate.ts` (CLI entry)
- `server/src/db/migrationRunner.ts` (idempotency + status check)

## Acceptance
- Running `migrate up` twice in a row is a no-op the second time (idempotent)
- Running `migrate status` lists applied + pending with timestamps
- Boot with `AUTO_MIGRATE=false` and pending migrations exits non-zero with a clear message
- Backup doc procedure is verified end-to-end on a sample dataset (dump → drop schema → restore → row counts match)

## Notes
- This is polish on top of the existing migration setup from F-07; do not redesign the runner unless the audit reveals a hard issue.
- Fully automated downward rollback ("migrate down") is OUT of scope — documented manual rollback notes are sufficient at MVP self-host.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §22 Risks, §23 step 10.

title: OSS-05: Desktop client — custom sync server URL setting (Settings → Account)
description:
## Goal
Allow the desktop client to connect to a self-hosted sync server by exposing a "Custom server URL" setting under Settings → Account, so users running their own infra can swap away from the hosted endpoint.

## Scope
- Settings → Account → Sync server section:
  - Default option: "Calmly hosted (recommended)" — uses the bundled hosted URL
  - Alternative: "Custom server URL" — text input accepting a full HTTPS URL
  - Validation: HTTPS only (refuse `http://` except `localhost` for development), URL format, trailing-slash normalization
  - "Test connection" button: hits `{url}/health` and `{url}/version`; shows pass/fail with a clear error if version mismatch with desktop client
- Switching the URL signs the user out (sessions are server-bound) and clears local sync state; warn clearly before switching
- Sync state cleared on switch: cached items remain in SQLite (read-only) until next sign-in repopulates from the new server; no data loss, just sync direction reset
- Persist setting in `UserSettings` (encrypted store not required — URL is not a secret)
- Surface the active server URL on the Sign-In screen subtly ("Connecting to: <url>") so users know which server they're authenticating against

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Account/SyncServerSection.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/sync/serverConfig.ts` (URL resolver: env override > user setting > bundled default)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/SignIn/SignIn.tsx` (show active server URL)
- `shared/src/config/serverUrl.ts` (validation + normalization)
- Migration: add `sync_server_url` field to user settings storage

## Acceptance
- Setting a valid custom URL + Test connection succeeds against a locally-running self-host (verified manually + e2e test against a stub server)
- HTTP URLs (non-localhost) are rejected with a clear error
- Switching URL warns about sign-out + sync reset; confirming clears session and reroutes to Sign In; cancelling leaves state unchanged
- Desktop with custom URL completes magic-link sign-in + a capture-to-review loop end-to-end against the self-hosted server
- Sign-In screen shows the active URL when it differs from the default

## Notes
- API version compatibility: client sends its `client-version`; server's `/version` is checked; mismatched majors show a friendly "Update Calmly or self-host server" message.
- This task pairs with `oss_dockerfile_compose` for the operator side.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging (optional self-host), §20 Architecture, §23 step 10.

title: OSS-06: Release pipeline — tagged GitHub releases, GHCR images, checksums
description:
## Goal
Stand up the release pipeline for the OSS sync server — tagged GitHub releases, container images published to GHCR, and SHA256 checksums — so operators can pin to a known-good version with verifiable artifacts.

## Scope
- GitHub Actions workflow `release.yml` triggered on tags matching `sync-v*`:
  - Build multi-arch container image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) via `docker/build-push-action`
  - Push to `ghcr.io/<org>/calmly-sync:<version>` and `:latest`
  - Generate SHA256 checksums for the image digest + any tarball artifacts
  - Create a GitHub Release with notes templated from a `CHANGELOG.md` section
  - Attach checksum file to the release
- Tag convention documented: `sync-v<semver>` (separate from desktop release tags)
- `CHANGELOG.md` at `server/CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep-a-Changelog; PRs that touch `server/` must update an "Unreleased" entry (lint check)
- Image signing via `cosign` (keyless OIDC) — optional for MVP; document the verification command if signing is enabled
- Release checklist `server/RELEASING.md`: bump version, update CHANGELOG, tag, monitor workflow, smoke-test pulled image
- Pre-release smoke test: a workflow job that pulls the freshly-pushed image and runs the docker-compose against it for `/health` and one migration cycle

## Files
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `server/CHANGELOG.md`
- `server/RELEASING.md`
- `.github/release-notes-template.md`
- `.github/workflows/changelog-lint.yml` (PR check that flags missing CHANGELOG entries)

## Acceptance
- Pushing a `sync-v0.1.0-test` tag triggers the workflow, produces a GHCR image, and creates a draft release with notes + checksums attached
- Pulling the published image and running `docker compose up` succeeds end-to-end
- CHANGELOG-lint check fails on a PR touching `server/` without an Unreleased entry
- `RELEASING.md` walks through a real release end-to-end (rehearsed once before close)

## Notes
- This task assumes the GitHub repo + GHCR org are set up; org-level config is operator concern, not coded here.
- Image signing is documented as a follow-up if cosign setup blocks the initial release.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging (open source release), §23 step 10, §26 (tension: cloud-first vs self-host).

title: OSS-07: Self-host smoke test (docker compose + AppImage + loop)
description:
## Goal
Self-host smoke test — clone OSS repo, `docker compose up`, point a fresh desktop client at it, sign in, and complete the daily loop. Validates the entire OSS-sync release path before tagging a release.

## Scope
- CI workflow `.github/workflows/oss-self-host.yml` (runs on tag pushes only)
- Steps:
  1. Spin up `docker-compose.yml` from the OSS sync repo (Postgres + sync server + Telegram bot stub) on a Linux GitHub runner
  2. Wait for `/health` → 200
  3. Configure a built desktop client (Linux AppImage from a recent main build) to point at `http://localhost:3001`
  4. Drive the client via Playwright: sign in (ConsoleEmailSender prints link → script reads it), capture an item, plan it, focus, mark done, review
  5. Tear down docker compose; assert clean shutdown
- Local dev script: `scripts/oss-smoke-test.sh` runs the same flow on a developer's machine
- Documentation: `docs/SELF_HOSTING.md` step-by-step matches what the smoke test exercises

## Files
- `.github/workflows/oss-self-host.yml`
- `scripts/oss-smoke-test.sh`
- `docs/SELF_HOSTING.md`
- `oss-sync/test/e2e/full-loop.spec.ts` (Playwright)

## Acceptance
- Workflow passes on the OSS-sync release tag
- Local script reproduces the workflow with `bash scripts/oss-smoke-test.sh`
- Docs walk a new operator from `git clone` to "loop completed" in under 10 minutes
- Tear-down leaves no orphan containers or volumes

## Skills
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger`** for the Playwright spec running against the AppImage on Linux — sandbox flags + display server (xvfb) configuration are skill-specific.

## Notes
- This task lives in the OSS-sync repo (extracted in OSS-01).
- It's the gate test before tagging an OSS release; ship-blocker.

## References
PRD §19 Pricing/Packaging, §20 Architecture, §26 Tensions Carried Forward.

title: AI v1.1: Ollama + OpenAI + hybrid + stuck rescue + daily planning
description:
## Goal
Expand AI to hybrid mode: add Ollama local provider, OpenAI as second cloud provider, hybrid routing UI, plus the two more demanding feature classes (stuck rescue, daily planning + replan suggestions).

## Build order
PRD §23 step 8 (AI v1.1).

## Scope
- Ollama local integration: detect Ollama running, list installed models, model picker in Settings
- OpenAI provider integration alongside Anthropic; key entry per provider
- Hybrid routing: per-action class default (triage=local, planning=cloud, etc.); user override; routing-rules editor
- Privacy mode toggle (Local-only / Allow cloud for selected actions)
- Suggestion behavior toggle (Automatic inline / On-demand only)
- "Speed vs quality" preference and "Show brief reason" toggle
- Stuck rescue AI suggestions in Focus
- Daily planning suggestions in Quick Plan / Plan
- Replan suggestions from Replan UI
- End-of-day / next-day suggestions in Review

## Out of scope
- Silent auto-rescheduling (PRD §8 explicitly out)
- Adaptive reminder AI (PRD §8)

## Done when
A user can pick Hybrid mode, configure both providers + Ollama, customize routing, and use all five higher-order AI actions (triage cleanup, Make Startable, brain-dump split, stuck rescue, daily planning) with inline failure paths.

## References
PRD §6 AI sub-modes, §16 AI Settings (full), §17 AI Technical Posture (Local Ollama + Hybrid + Fallback), §22 Risks (model variance, latency).

title: AI11-01: Ollama integration (detect daemon, list models, picker in Settings, provider impl)
description:
## Goal
Integrate Ollama as a local AI provider: detect a running Ollama daemon, list installed models, expose a model picker in Settings, and ship a concrete `AIProvider` implementation that plugs into the orchestration layer from Epic 7.

## Scope
- Detection: HTTP probe to `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags` with a 1s timeout; cached for 30s
- Model list: parse `/api/tags` response into `{ name, size, family }[]`
- Generation: implement `OllamaProvider` against `/api/generate` (or `/api/chat`); JSON-mode for structured prompts
- Settings → AI page additions:
  - Status row: "Ollama detected" / "Ollama not running [How to install]"
  - Model picker (dropdown of installed models) — persists to `user_settings.ai.localModel`
  - "Refresh" button forces re-detection
  - Disabled options from Epic 7 (`Local only`, `Hybrid`) are now enabled
- Failure cases mapped to existing `AIError` shape:
  - Ollama not running → `network` with copy "Start Ollama to use Local AI"
  - No models installed → `invalid_response` with copy "Pull a model with `ollama pull <name>`"
  - Generation timeout → `timeout`

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/providers/ollama.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/ollamaDetect.ts` — detection + model list with cache
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/aiSettings.ts` — extend with `getOllamaStatus`, `listOllamaModels`
- `desktop/src/preload/aiSettings.ts` — extend bridge
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/settings/AIPage.tsx` — extend with status + picker
- `shared/src/model/settings.ts` — extend `ai` schema with `localModel`
- Unit test: `desktop/src/main/ai/__tests__/ollama.test.ts` (mock fetch)

## Acceptance
- With Ollama running, the picker shows installed models from `/api/tags`
- With Ollama stopped, the status row shows "not running" and Local/Hybrid modes are gated
- Selecting a model persists across restart
- A `runAI` call routed to Ollama (forced via test harness) returns a structured response
- Stopping Ollama mid-call surfaces `network` error via existing failure banner

## Notes
- The app does NOT bundle Ollama or any model. Recommend Gemma 2 2B / Llama 3.2 3B / Phi-3.5 mini in copy (PRD §17).
- Local provider must conform to the same `AIProvider` interface from `ai1_orchestration` — no new abstractions.
- Local model output is highly variable; rely on Zod validation to bounce malformed structured outputs.

## References
PRD §17 AI Technical Posture (Local Ollama), §16 AI Settings (Local model picker), §22 Risks (local model variance).

title: AI11-10: AI v1.1 integration test (Ollama+OpenAI mocks, routing, privacy)
description:
## Goal
Integration test pass for AI v1.1 — Ollama + OpenAI mocks, hybrid routing, privacy mode, and the four advanced action classes (stuck rescue, daily planning, replan, end-of-day).

## Scope
- Mock Ollama HTTP API (`desktop/test/mocks/ollama.ts`) — `/api/tags` and `/api/generate`
- Mock OpenAI Chat Completions (`desktop/test/mocks/openai.ts`)
- Reuse Anthropic mock from AI1-09
- Specs:
  1. **Ollama detection**: mock running Ollama with 2 models → Settings model picker shows them
  2. **Ollama not running**: mock returns connection refused → inline message + "Start Ollama" hint, Cloud actions still work
  3. **OpenAI configuration**: enter key → key encrypted, validation call to mocked OpenAI succeeds
  4. **Hybrid routing default**: triage action → Ollama mock receives the call (not Anthropic/OpenAI); planning action → cloud mock receives
  5. **Routing override**: user maps triage → cloud → triage now goes to cloud
  6. **Privacy mode Local-only**: planning action attempted → blocked with friendly message; no cloud calls made
  7. **Stuck rescue**: in Focus, click "I'm stuck" → AI tier suggests a 1-line nudge → user can accept/edit/reject
  8. **Daily planning**: in Quick Plan, "Suggest my day" → AI returns ordered list → drop-in to today's plan with one click; reorder before commit
  9. **Replan**: in Replan UI, "Suggest changes" → AI proposes shrink/move/drop ops → user accepts subset
  10. **End-of-day**: in Review, "What's tomorrow's top item?" → AI returns one item → optional accept
  11. **Speed-vs-quality preference**: setting changes affect prompt selection (verify via mock-recorded prompt)
  12. **Show-reason toggle**: when on, suggestions include a one-line rationale
- Real-AI cassette suite extended with a small Ollama smoke test (only runs locally with Ollama installed)

## Files
- `desktop/test/integration/ai-v11/{ollama-detection,ollama-down,openai-config,routing-default,routing-override,privacy-local,stuck,daily-plan,replan,end-of-day,speed-quality,show-reason}.spec.ts`
- `desktop/test/mocks/{ollama.ts,openai.ts}`

## Acceptance
- All twelve specs pass with mocks
- Routing default plus per-action override demonstrably swaps providers
- Privacy mode hard-blocks all cloud calls — no fallback that silently exfiltrates
- Speed-vs-quality preference observably changes prompt class selection (assert via mock recorder)

## Skills
**Invoke `claude-api`** when the orchestration code wraps Anthropic; confirm the SDK pattern, prompt caching, and latest model IDs.
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger`** for renderer-driven Playwright specs (settings UI, advanced action accept flows).

## Notes
- Tests must be deterministic — no live model calls in CI.
- Avoid coupling the routing implementation to a specific HTTP client; the mock should work with any.

## References
PRD §6 (full sub-modes), §16 AI Settings, §17 (Local Ollama + Hybrid + Fallback), §13 Error states.

title: AI11-03: Hybrid routing config (per-action defaults + user override + Settings editor)
description:
## Goal
Implement hybrid routing: a per-action-class mapping of where each AI prompt class runs (Local / Cloud / specific provider), with shipped defaults and a Settings UI to edit the rules.

## Scope
- Routing config shape:
  ```ts
  type ActionClass =
    | 'triage_cleanup' | 'make_startable' | 'brain_dump_split'
    | 'stuck_rescue' | 'daily_planning' | 'replan' | 'end_of_day'
  type Destination = 'local' | 'cloud:anthropic' | 'cloud:openai'
  type RoutingRules = Record<ActionClass, Destination>
  ```
- Shipped defaults (per PRD §17 hybrid intent):
  - `triage_cleanup` → local
  - `make_startable` → local
  - `brain_dump_split` → local
  - `stuck_rescue` → cloud (default cloud provider)
  - `daily_planning` → cloud
  - `replan` → cloud
  - `end_of_day` → cloud
- Resolves `cloud:anthropic` / `cloud:openai` literally; resolves bare `cloud` to user's default cloud provider
- `runAI` consults `RoutingRules` first, then mode (Off / Local only / Cloud only / Hybrid):
  - Local only forces destination to local regardless of rule
  - Cloud only forces destination to default cloud
  - Hybrid honors the rule
- Settings UI: routing-rules editor with one dropdown per ActionClass listing valid destinations (limited by what's configured: hide local options if no Ollama model picked, hide cloud options if no key)
- Per-rule "Reset to default" and a top-level "Reset all" affordance

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/routing.ts` — defaults + resolver

title: Foundations: Electron shell, auth, storage, sync skeleton
description:
## Goal
Stand up the technical foundation the rest of the build depends on: an Electron desktop app with a SQLite local cache, magic-link auth, a hosted-sync server skeleton, and a defined sync protocol — all wired so subsequent feature epics can plug into them.

title: F-11: Sync protocol v1 — server endpoints + client queue + offline replay
description:
## Goal
Implement sync protocol v1: cloud-first source of truth with local-cache reads, an offline write queue that replays on reconnect, and last-write-wins conflict resolution per record. This is the spine that every feature epic relies on.

## Scope
- Protocol shape: each domain table has `id` (uuid), `updated_at` (ms), `deleted_at` NULL (soft-delete), `version` (monotonic int from server)
- Server endpoints:
  - `POST /sync/pull` body `{ since: <version> }` → returns `{ records: { tasks: [...], inbox_items: [...], ... }, version: <new> }`
  - `POST /sync/push` body `{ ops: [{ table, op: 'upsert'|'delete', payload }] }` → server applies, bumps `version`, returns `{ accepted: [...], rejected: [{op, reason}], version }`
- Client (desktop) maintains:
  - `op_queue` table (id, table, op, payload_json, created_at, attempts, last_error)
  - `sync_state` (last_pulled_version, last_pushed_at)
  - Background loop: try push pending ops, then pull, on any network event or every 30s
- Offline behavior: reads always hit local cache; writes go to local cache + op_queue immediately; push is best-effort
- Conflict resolution: server LWW by `updated_at`; client surfaces no UI conflict (acceptable for MVP single-user multi-device)
- Reconnect: when network returns, drain op_queue with exponential backoff

## Files
- `server/src/sync/{routes.ts,apply.ts,pull.ts,version.ts}`
- `desktop/src/main/sync/{client.ts,queue.ts,loop.ts}`
- Migrations: `server/migrations/0003_sync.sql` (add version cols + sync_log if helpful), `desktop/.../0004_op_queue.sql`

## Acceptance
- E2E: write task offline → reconnect → record appears on a second client after pull
- Pull is idempotent: same `since` returns same set
- Push is idempotent: replaying the same op queue does not duplicate records (use client-generated UUIDs)
- Backoff: failed pushes don't busy-loop (1s, 2s, 4s, ... cap 60s)
- Soft-deletes propagate

## Notes
- This protocol is intentionally simple. A real CRDT is overkill at MVP; LWW + soft-delete handles single-user multi-device.

title: F-12: Encrypted-at-rest secret store (Electron safeStorage helper)
description:
## Goal
Provide a secure, OS-keychain-backed encryption helper for sensitive fields (API keys, OAuth refresh tokens, session cookies) so they're never persisted in plaintext on disk.

## Scope
- Wrapper around Electron `safeStorage`:
  - `encryptString(plain: string): Buffer`
  - `decryptString(cipher: Buffer): string`
  - Behavior on unsupported platforms: surface a clear `EncryptionUnavailable` error so callers can refuse to persist
- A typed "secret store" facade:
  - `secretStore.set(key: SecretKey, value: string)`
  - `secretStore.get(key: SecretKey): string | null`
  - `secretStore.delete(key: SecretKey)`
  - Backed by SQLite: `secrets(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ciphertext BLOB, updated_at INTEGER)`
- Key namespacing: `auth.session`, `ai.anthropic.key`, `ai.openai.key`, `calendar.google.refresh_token:<account_id>`, etc.
- Roundtrip helpers exposed to renderer via narrow IPC (renderer never sees raw bytes; renderer asks "is the Anthropic key set?" or "store this key" and "use the key to call X" — never exfiltrate)

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/security/safeStorage.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/security/secretStore.ts`
- Migration: `desktop/.../0005_secrets.sql`
- `desktop/src/preload/secrets.ts` — narrow API: `setKey`, `hasKey`, `clearKey` (no `getKey`)

## Acceptance
- Roundtrip a value: `set('ai.anthropic.key', 'sk-...')` then `get(...)` returns the same string
- DB inspection shows ciphertext, not plaintext
- On a platform without secure backing (e.g., headless Linux), the helper throws `EncryptionUnavailable` and callers handle it (block-with-clear-message)
- Renderer cannot read a secret value directly — only ask the main process to perform an action with it

## Notes
- This is the single chokepoint for "things we promised are encrypted at rest" in PRD §14 structural notes.
- Keep the renderer-facing API surface tight to limit blast radius if the renderer is compromised.

## References
PRD §14 (structural notes: API keys encrypted at rest, never sent to server in plaintext), §17 (BYO key), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach:
- Thin wrapper around Electron safeStorage (encryptString/decryptString) that throws a typed EncryptionUnavailableError on platforms with no secure backing OR Linux 'basic_text' fallback (we treat the fallback as insecure).
- DB-backed secretStore facade in main with set/get/has/delete on a new secrets(key TEXT PK, ciphertext BLOB, updated_at INT) STRICT table — migration 0004_secrets.sql (next free slot; spec mentioned 0005 informally).
- Type-safe SecretKey union: static keys (auth.session, ai.anthropic.key, ai.openai.key) plus parameterized template-literal keys for calendar refresh tokens. Runtime validator (isValidSecretKey) used at the IPC boundary so renderer cannot persist arbitrary keys.
- Renderer-facing IPC is intentionally narrow: setKey, hasKey, clearKey only — NO getKey. Plaintext never crosses the IPC boundary; downstream features (Anthropic SDK, calendar fetch) call secretStore.get() in main and use the value to perform a specific action whose result is what the renderer sees.
- Self-test: secretStoreSelfTest() runs at app whenReady in dev mode, encrypts a token, persists, reads back raw bytes (asserts ciphertext != plaintext), decrypts (asserts roundtrip), cleans up. Logs [calmly:secrets] ok/unavailable/failed. Cheap empirical proof on every dev launch.

Tradeoffs: NOT exposing getKey via IPC (this is the whole point — narrow blast radius). NOT using a per-secret AAD/AEAD (safeStorage's underlying primitive already handles that). NOT writing formal Vitest tests (Electron-runtime + OS-keychain dependent — F-03 will own those). NOT building a key-rotation flow yet — values are upserted with ON CONFLICT.

Skill: playwright-electron-debugger noted in the bead but the test harness lands later in F-03; current iteration covers main + IPC + preload only.
close_reason: Encrypted-at-rest secret store live. Migration 0004_secrets.sql lands the secrets(key,ciphertext,updated_at) STRICT table. safeStorage wrapper throws typed EncryptionUnavailableError on platforms without secure backing (incl. Linux basic_text fallback). secretStore facade in main exposes set/get/has/delete with type-safe SecretKey union (auth.session, ai.anthropic.key, ai.openai.key, calendar.{google,microsoft}.refresh_token:<id>) — runtime allowlist + bounded-charset regex on parameterized keys validates IPC input. Renderer-facing IPC is intentionally narrow: setKey, hasKey, clearKey only. NO getKey — plaintext never crosses the IPC boundary. Self-test runs at whenReady in dev: cold-boot logged 'selftest ok=true available=true cipherDifferent=true roundtrip=true' on Windows DPAPI, proving the full encrypt → persist → read raw bytes → decrypt path works AND that ciphertext bytes differ from plaintext bytes. Self-test cleans up its row. Note: formal Vitest+Playwright tests for cross-platform coverage (incl. Linux basic_text rejection) deferred to F-03 infra.

title: F-13: Structured logging + crash reporting infra (PII-aware, opt-in upload)
description:
## Goal
Set up structured, PII-aware logging and crash reporting infrastructure on both desktop and server so future failures are diagnosable without leaking task content, calendar content, Telegram message content, or API keys.

## Scope

- Desktop renderer: console wrapper that forwards via IPC to main; never logs message text
- A `logger.event(name, props)` helper with strict prop allowlist (booleans, ints, enum strings) to make accidental PII leak harder
- Crash reporting: Electron `crashReporter` configured with `uploadToServer: false` by default — opt-in flips it on (Epic 9 owns the toggle UI)

- `desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts`
- `server/src/logging/index.ts` (consumes pino redaction)

## Acceptance

- Logger does not write any field outside the allow-list when called via `logger.event`
- Crash report toggle defaults to OFF; flipping it ON only takes effect after restart (acceptable; documented)

## Notes
- This is the deterministic spine for telemetry; the actual opt-in telemetry pipeline is Epic 9.
- Allow PII in DEBUG-only paths gated by `LOG_PII=true` env var, hard-disabled in prod builds.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry (never captures task/calendar/Telegram content/API keys), §22 risks (latency surfaces), §23 step 1.

title: F-04: SQLite local cache (better-sqlite3) with migration runner + FTS5
description:
## Goal
Add a SQLite local cache to the desktop app using `better-sqlite3`, with a migration runner and FTS5 enabled, so subsequent epics can persist data locally and Search (Epic 6) can index against the same DB.

## Scope
- Add `better-sqlite3` to `desktop/` (rebuilt against Electron via `@electron/rebuild` or `electron-rebuild`)
- DB lives in `app.getPath('userData')/calmly.db`
- Migration runner: numbered SQL files in `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/` applied in order; `_meta` table tracks applied versions
- Pragmas at boot: `journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, `temp_store=MEMORY`
- Compile/load FTS5 extension (it's built into better-sqlite3 by default)
- Expose typed query helpers in `desktop/src/main/db/index.ts`
- Expose limited DB operations to renderer via preload IPC (read/write specific shapes — never raw SQL)

## Files to create
- `desktop/src/main/db/index.ts` — open + migration runner
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0001_init.sql` — placeholder (real schema lands in F-05)
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0002_fts.sql` — placeholder for FTS5 trigger pattern (real index in Epic 6)
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/db.ts` — IPC handlers
- `desktop/src/preload/db.ts` — typed bridge
- Update `electron.vite.config.ts` to externalize `better-sqlite3`

## Acceptance
- App boots, opens DB at userData path, runs migrations idempotently
- WAL mode confirmed via `PRAGMA journal_mode`
- FTS5 available: `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(...)` succeeds
- Renderer can call `window.calmly.db.health()` and get `{ ok: true, version: <migration n> }`

## Notes
- Native module rebuild is the most fragile part on Windows — document the postinstall step.
- Do not write any business-domain tables here; that's F-05.

## References
PRD §11 Search (FTS5), §20 Architecture (local cache), §23 step 1.
notes:
Approach:
- better-sqlite3 11.x as the local store, opened in main only; renderer never holds the connection.
- Migration runner: numbered SQL files bundled at build via Vite's import.meta.glob('./migrations/*.sql', {query:'?raw', import:'default', eager:true}). Runner creates _meta_migrations(version,name,applied_at) on first boot, applies unapplied files in a single transaction each, idempotent.
- Pragmas applied at boot: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, temp_store=MEMORY.
- Native rebuild: @electron/rebuild as devDep + postinstall script on the desktop workspace; .npmrc enable-pre-post-scripts=true so pnpm honors it. Falls back to prebuild-install when binaries are available.
- IPC surface: ipcMain.handle('db:health') returns {ok, version}. Preload exposes window.calmly.db.health() via a typed dbBridge merged into the existing CalmlyApi.

Tradeoffs: NOT writing domain schema (F-05 owns that). NOT building a query builder or ORM — bare prepared statements. Migrations are forward-only (no down migrations) — keeps the runner small; if we ever need rollback we'll add it then. NOT exposing raw SQL to the renderer (security: only typed IPC handlers).

Verification: boot app, confirm DB file at userData path, journal_mode=wal, FTS5 virtual table create succeeds in 0002, health() returns version=2.
close_reason: SQLite cache live. better-sqlite3 11.5.0 rebuilt against Electron 32 ABI via @electron/rebuild. Migration runner uses Vite import.meta.glob to bundle SQL at build time; runs unapplied .sql files in order inside per-migration transactions. _meta_migrations table tracks applied versions. Boot smoke test: cold start logged 'version=2 appliedNow=[1,2]', second boot logged 'appliedNow=[]' confirming idempotency. FTS5 demonstrated by 0002 creating CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE _fts5_smoketest USING fts5(content) without error. WAL/synchronous=NORMAL/foreign_keys=ON/temp_store=MEMORY pragmas applied at open. IPC: ipcMain.handle('db:health') registered; renderer can call window.calmly.db.health() via preload contextBridge; Home.tsx surfaces {version, walMode, fts5} as a status pill so future launch visibly demonstrates the round-trip. Note: install requires --ignore-scripts followed by pnpm rebuild-native (or postinstall when conditions allow) due to Node 24 system version vs better-sqlite3 prebuilds; documented via the desktop rebuild-native script.

title: F-05: Core data-model schema (SQLite migrations + Zod types in shared)
description:
## Goal
Implement the core data-model schema (PRD §14) as SQLite migrations and parallel TypeScript types/Zod schemas in `@calmly/shared`, so all downstream epics work against a single canonical model.

## Scope
SQL tables (in a new migration `0003_core_model.sql`):
- `users` — id, email, magic_link_token (transient), created_at
- `inbox_items` — id, user_id, raw_text, source ('desktop' | 'telegram-text' | 'telegram-voice' | 'ai-split'), created_at, resolved_at NULL
- `tasks` — id, user_id, title, notes, type, status ('open'|'in_progress'|'done'|'dropped'|'snoozed'), due_at NULL, parent_task_id NULL, source, created_at, updated_at
- `events` — id, user_id, title, start_at, end_at, source ('manual'|'calendar-import'), created_at
- `reminder_rules` — id, task_id, importance ('important'|'soft'), interval_seconds, escalation_json, active
- `recurrence_rules` — id, owner_type ('task'|'reminder'), owner_id, rrule_text
- `calendar_event_imports` — id, user_id, provider ('google'|'microsoft'), external_id, raw_json, start_at, end_at, last_seen_at
- `ai_suggestions` — id, owner_type, owner_id, model, prompt_class, suggestion_json, outcome ('accepted'|'rejected'|'edited'|'pending'), created_at
- `telegram_links` — id, user_id, chat_id, linked_at
- `user_settings` — user_id PK, settings_json (versioned schema)

Shared layer (`shared/src/model/`):
- Zod schemas mirroring each table
- TypeScript types exported (`Task`, `InboxItem`, etc.)
- Enum unions exported (`TaskStatus`, `Source`, `ReminderImportance`, etc.)

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0003_core_model.sql`
- `shared/src/model/task.ts`, `inbox.ts`, `event.ts`, `reminder.ts`, `recurrence.ts`, `calendar.ts`, `ai.ts`, `telegram.ts`, `settings.ts`, `user.ts`
- `shared/src/model/index.ts` re-exports

## Acceptance
- Migration applies cleanly on a fresh DB
- `pnpm -r test` includes a unit test that round-trips one row of each table via the typed query helper
- Zod schemas reject invalid inputs (e.g., bad enum, missing required fields)
- All foreign keys cascade-correctly (e.g., deleting a user deletes their inbox/tasks)

## Notes
- Tasks support parent_task_id from day one (PRD §14 structural notes); MVP UI exposes one level only.
- `settings_json` evolution is handled by versioning the schema inside the JSON, not adding columns.
- Encryption of secret fields (API keys, OAuth tokens) is **not** in this task — that's F-12; here we just leave the columns/JSON paths for them.

## References
PRD §14 Data Model Sketch (full).
notes:
Approach:
- 0003_core_model.sql: 10 STRICT tables with TEXT UUID PKs, INTEGER (unix ms) timestamps via unixepoch()*1000, CHECK constraints for enum-like columns, FK CASCADE for user-owned children. JSON columns guarded by json_valid(). magic_link_token stored as token_hash + expires_at (PRD says transient — never store raw).
- shared/src/model/*.ts: one file per table — Zod schema + inferred TS type + exported enum unions. Raw zod (no transform) so storage shape and domain shape align — the JSON columns stay as strings at this layer and the domains that own them (reminders, settings, calendar) tighten in their own epics.
- shared adds zod 3.23.x as a runtime dep + vitest as a devDep + a vitest config + Zod-only validation tests (acceptance + rejection).

Tradeoffs: NOT writing the DB round-trip test in this bead (depends on F-03 / Vitest infra and Node-ABI better-sqlite3) — split into F-05b. NOT typing the contents of escalation_json / settings_json / suggestion_json at this layer; those tighten when their owning epics land. NOT encrypting any field — F-12 owns secret encryption. Verifying 0003 applies on a fresh DB via the existing Electron boot smoke test.

Skill: none — pure schema + Zod work, no UI or AI calls.
close_reason: Core data-model schema landed. 0003_core_model.sql defines 10 STRICT tables (users, inbox_items, tasks, events, reminder_rules, recurrence_rules, calendar_event_imports, ai_suggestions, telegram_links, user_settings) with TEXT UUID PKs, INTEGER unix-ms timestamps, CHECK constraints on all enum-like columns, json_valid() guards on JSON columns, FK CASCADE for user-owned children, and indexes on common access paths. Per-table Zod schemas in shared/src/model/* with inferred TS types — exported as @calmly/shared/model. 21 Zod validation tests in shared/src/model/__tests__/schemas.test.ts cover happy + sad paths for every table (bad uuids, bad emails, unknown enum values, malformed JSON, non-positive intervals, end_at<start_at). Migration applies cleanly on a fresh DB: cold-boot smoke test logged 'version=3 appliedNow=[1,2,3]'. DB round-trip + cascade test split into F-05b (calmly-hju) since it needs F-03's Vitest-with-better-sqlite3 infra. Magic-link token kept as token_hash + expires_at — raw token never persists.

Approach:
- Fastify v5 (typed, fast, ships with pino) + node-postgres (pg) pool wrapper. Skipping ORMs at this stage — raw SQL via the pool is enough until F-08/F-11 land real domain queries.
- Migrations via node-pg-migrate, .cjs files in server/migrations/. Placeholder 0001 migration just to wire the runner; real schema lands in F-08.

title: F-08: Magic-link auth — server endpoints (request, redeem, session)
description:
## Goal
Implement the server side of magic-link auth: request a link by email, redeem the token to a session, and protect API routes with session middleware.

## Scope
- Add Postgres tables in a new migration:
  - `users` (id, email UNIQUE, created_at)
  - `magic_link_tokens` (token, user_id, expires_at, consumed_at NULL, requested_ip)
  - `sessions` (id, user_id, expires_at, last_used_at, user_agent)
- Endpoints:
  - `POST /auth/magic-link/request` body `{ email }` — creates user if absent, generates token (32-byte random base64url), stores hash + expiry (15 min), enqueues email send (adapter from F-09), rate-limited per email/IP
  - `POST /auth/magic-link/redeem` body `{ token }` — validates, consumes (idempotent), returns `{ session: { id, expiresAt } }` and sets HttpOnly cookie
  - `POST /auth/logout` — invalidates session
  - `GET /auth/me` — returns `{ user: { id, email } }` if session valid
- Session middleware: validates cookie, rejects with 401 otherwise
- All token comparisons use constant-time equality

## Files
- `server/migrations/0002_auth.sql`
- `server/src/auth/{routes.ts,session.ts,tokens.ts,rate-limit.ts}`
- `server/src/middleware/requireSession.ts`

## Acceptance
- Unit tests cover: token expiry, idempotent redeem, rate-limit, session cookie flags (HttpOnly, Secure in prod, SameSite=Lax)
- Integration test: full request → redeem → me → logout flow against real Postgres (testcontainers)
- Tokens are stored hashed (sha256), never plaintext, in DB
- Session cookies are HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Secure (prod)

## Notes
- Email send is stubbed via the F-09 adapter; this task does not own the adapter.
- Replay protection: `magic_link_tokens.consumed_at` blocks reuse.
- Rate limit example: 5 requests / hour per email, 20 / hour per IP.

## References
PRD §12 Onboarding (magic link), §20 Architecture, §23 step 1.

title: Reminders engine: two-tier importance, intervals, Telegram + desktop
description:
## Goal
Implement the reminders engine: Important/Soft tiers, user-defined repeat intervals, scheduling, dispatch via Telegram (when linked) with Done/Snooze/Reschedule action buttons, and desktop notification fallback.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 4 (Reminders engine).

## Scope
- ReminderRule data model behavior (schema lives in Epic 1)
- Per-task reminder profile + per-profile defaults in Settings
- Interval scheduler (e.g., every 10m until ack, every 4h, daily) — server-side worker
- Telegram delivery channel: send messages with inline Done/Snooze 10m/Reschedule buttons
- Desktop notification channel as fallback when Telegram not linked
- Inline action handlers (Done closes, Snooze reschedules, Reschedule opens picker)
- "Important" vs "Soft" rendering differences
- Settings → Reminders page: profile editor, defaults

## Out of scope
- Four-tier reminder profiles (PRD §8 explicitly out)
- Adaptive reminder AI (PRD §8)
- WhatsApp/SMS channels (PRD §8)

## Done when
A user can attach a reminder to a task with importance + interval, get pushed to Telegram or desktop, and resolve via Done/Snooze/Reschedule.

## References
PRD §11 Reminders, §7 desktop item 8, §8 Out of Scope (four-tier, WhatsApp/SMS).

title: RM-01: ReminderRule UI + per-task reminder editor
description:
## Goal

  - **Repeat behavior**: "Until I mark Done" (Important default) vs "Once" (Soft default)
  - **Escalation** (Important only): toggle "Bring window forward each repeat" (no system-modal hijack — we are not Windscribe)
  - **Start at**: optional datetime; default = now
- Save → POST/PUT to `/tasks/:id/reminder-rule`; remove → DELETE

title: RM-03: Server-side scheduler/dispatcher worker (interval + dedupe + retry)
description:
## Goal
Build the server-side reminder scheduler/dispatcher worker: wakes on an interval, finds due `ReminderRule` instances, dispatches one notification per due fire, dedupes within a window, retries on transient failure, and records delivery state.

## Scope
- New worker `server/src/reminders/scheduler.ts` running in the same Node process as the API (Fastify plugin with a `setInterval` driver, default tick = 30s)
- Computes next-fire time per rule based on `start_at`, `interval_min`, `last_fired_at`, `repeat_until_done`
- New table `reminder_deliveries` (id, rule_id, user_id, scheduled_for, fired_at nullable, channel, status enum: pending/sent/failed/skipped/acked, attempt_count, last_error)
- Dedupe: do not fire if a `pending` or `sent` delivery exists within the rule's interval/2
- Channel selection logic (interface only — channels themselves in rm04 + rm05): asks `ChannelRouter.pickChannel(userId)` → returns `'telegram' | 'desktop'`; calls `Channel.deliver(delivery)`
- Retry: on `Channel.deliver` failure, increment `attempt_count`; up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 15m); then mark `failed` and emit domain event
- Stop firing rule when associated task is `done` or `archived`
- Manual cancel: `POST /reminder-deliveries/:id/cancel`
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM (finish in-flight ticks, persist state)
- Time math uses UTC internally; rule storage uses UTC
- Telemetry counters: `reminders_fired`, `reminders_failed`, `reminders_acked`

## Files
- `server/migrations/00xx_reminder_deliveries.sql`
- `server/src/reminders/scheduler.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/router.ts` (ChannelRouter interface + impl)
- `server/src/reminders/channels/types.ts` (Channel interface)
- `server/src/reminders/state.ts` (next-fire computation, pure functions)
- Tests: `server/src/reminders/scheduler.test.ts` (uses fake timers + mock channels)

## Acceptance
- A rule with `interval_min=10`, `start_at=now-1min` fires once on next tick; the next fire is scheduled 10 min later
- A rule for a `done` task does NOT fire
- Dedupe: triggering two ticks within the same interval does not produce two deliveries
- Failed delivery retries up to 3 times then marks `failed` and emits the domain event
- Tick performance: a 1k-rule scenario completes within 1s on the test runner
- Worker shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM (test asserts no in-flight delivery is duplicated on restart)

## Notes
- Channels are wired by rm04 (Telegram) and rm05 (desktop). Until both land, use a `LogChannel` for tests.
- Distributed locking is not needed at MVP scale — single-process worker is fine. Document as a follow-up risk in scheduler.ts header.
- Calendar reminders (event-time triggers) are out of scope here; only `ReminderRule`-driven.

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (delivery, intervals), §22 Risks, §23 step 4.

title: RM-04: Telegram delivery channel (Done / Snooze / Reschedule buttons)
description:
## Goal
Implement the Telegram delivery channel: takes a `reminder_delivery` row, sends a Telegram message via the outbound infrastructure (Epic 3 tg07), with inline buttons Done / Snooze 10m / Reschedule.

## Scope
- `server/src/reminders/channels/telegram.ts` implementing `Channel` interface
- Message text format:
  - Important: `🔔 *<task title>*\nNext: <next step or '—'>`
  - Soft: `<task title>` (no bell, no bold)
- Buttons (inline, via tg07's `sendMessage`):
  - `Done` → action `reminder.done` with payload `{ deliveryId, taskId }`
  - `Snooze 10m` → action `reminder.snooze` payload `{ deliveryId, minutes: 10 }`
  - `Reschedule` → action `reminder.reschedule` payload `{ deliveryId, taskId }`
- On `TelegramNotLinkedError` from outbound infra: return `{ ok: false, fallback: true }` so router falls back to desktop channel (rm05)
- On Telegram 403 (user blocked bot): same fallback signal + emit domain event (already emitted by tg07; this channel just respects it)
- On other errors: return `{ ok: false, fallback: false }` so scheduler retries
- Updates `reminder_deliveries.status` to `sent` and stores `outbound_message_id` for callback correlation

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/channels/telegram.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/router.ts` (extend: prefer Telegram if linked, else desktop)
- Tests: `server/src/reminders/channels/telegram.test.ts` (mock outbound)

## Acceptance
- Linked user with Important rule receives a bold/bell-prefixed message with all three buttons
- Linked user with Soft rule receives plain message with all three buttons
- Unlinked user → channel returns fallback signal, no message sent
- Blocked user → channel returns fallback signal, delivery marked appropriately
- `reminder_deliveries.outbound_message_id` is populated on success
- Tests verify correct payload shapes for each button

## Notes
- Action handlers (the Done/Snooze/Reschedule logic) are in rm06 — this task only ships the send side.
- Edit-on-snooze (greying out buttons after press) is rm06.
- Depends on tg07 (outbound infra) and rm03 (Channel interface + scheduler).

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (Telegram delivery, action buttons), §7 Telegram bot.

title: RM-05: Desktop notification fallback channel
description:
## Goal
Implement the desktop notification fallback channel: when Telegram is unlinked or fallback is signaled, deliver a reminder via Electron's native notification API with Done / Snooze / Reschedule actions.

## Scope
- New IPC channel `reminders:incoming` from main → renderer
- Server-to-desktop transport: piggyback on the existing sync stream (Epic 1 F-11) — push a `pending_reminder` event to the connected desktop client; client acks
- Main process: receives the event via the sync transport; calls `new Notification({ title, body, actions })`
  - Important: title prefixed with bell, sticky if platform supports
  - Soft: standard notification
  - Three actions: Done / Snooze / Reschedule (Windows uses Action Center buttons; macOS uses notification actions; Linux best-effort)
- Click on notification body opens the desktop app to the task's Focus or detail page
- Action click → POSTs to `/reminder-deliveries/:id/action` with `{ action }` — server handles via rm06's action registry
- If desktop client is offline (no live sync connection), reminder remains `pending`; on reconnect, undelivered reminders within last 30 min are flushed
- New table column `reminder_deliveries.desktop_acked_at` for desktop-side ack tracking

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/channels/desktop.ts`
- `server/src/sync/events.ts` (extend with `pending_reminder` event type)
- `desktop/src/main/reminders/notifier.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/reminders/index.ts` (subscribe to sync events, dispatch to notifier)
- `desktop/src/renderer/state/reminders.ts` (action invocation helper)
- `server/migrations/00xx_desktop_acked.sql`
- Tests: server channel test, desktop notifier unit test (mock Notification)

## Acceptance
- Unlinked user with a fired rule receives a desktop notification with three action buttons
- Clicking Done sends the action POST and the notification dismisses
- Offline desktop client: reminder remains pending; on reconnect within 30 min, notification fires
- Important reminders use bell prefix; Soft do not
- Notifications respect OS-level Do Not Disturb (no special override — we are not Windscribe — per rm07 intrusion design)

## Notes
- Native notifications on Windows require an AppUserModelID and packaged app; in dev, fall back to a basic toast and log a warning.
- Linux notification action support is patchy — fallback is to open the app on click and let the user resolve there.
- Per PRD §8: WhatsApp/SMS channels are out of scope.

## References
PRD §7 Reminders (desktop notification fallback), §11 Reminders (delivery), §13 Error states.

title: RM-06: Inline action handlers (Done / Snooze / Reschedule)
description:
## Goal
Wire the inline action handlers for reminder Done / Snooze / Reschedule, called from both Telegram callbacks and desktop notification action POSTs.

## Scope
- `server/src/reminders/actions.ts` — three handler functions:
  - `handleDone({ deliveryId })`: marks delivery `acked`, marks the underlying rule `done` (stop further fires), marks task complete only if user opted in via setting (default: NO — Done acks the reminder, not the task; explicit per PRD calmness principle). Edits/replaces the original Telegram message to "Done ✓ <title>" with no buttons.
  - `handleSnooze({ deliveryId, minutes })`: marks delivery `snoozed`, schedules a fresh delivery `now + minutes`. Edits original message to "Snoozed until <HH:mm> — <title>" with no buttons.
  - `handleReschedule({ deliveryId, taskId })`: marks delivery `acked`. For Telegram: opens a date-picker mini-flow — sends a follow-up message with date chips (Today evening, Tomorrow, In 2 days, This weekend, Custom). For desktop: deep-links into desktop app's task detail with the date picker focused.
- Register all three with both:
  - Telegram action registry from tg07
  - HTTP route `POST /reminder-deliveries/:id/action` (for desktop)
- Idempotency: pressing Done twice (e.g., user clicks both Telegram and desktop notification) is a no-op on the second call
- Update `reminder_deliveries.status` and `acked_at`
- Audit log: each action records actor (telegram/desktop) + timestamp

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/actions.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/handlers/done.ts`, `snooze.ts`, `reschedule.ts`
- `server/src/reminders/routes.ts` (add `/reminder-deliveries/:id/action`)
- `server/src/telegram/actions.ts` (register handlers — uses registry from tg07)
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/RescheduleDeepLink.tsx` (handles `calmly://reschedule/<taskId>`)
- Tests for each handler covering idempotency, edit-message behavior, snooze re-scheduling

## Acceptance
- Pressing Done in Telegram: original message becomes "Done ✓ <title>", delivery row `acked`, no further fires
- Pressing Snooze 10m: original message becomes "Snoozed until …", a new delivery is scheduled 10 min later, fires correctly
- Pressing Reschedule (Telegram): user receives the date-chip follow-up; selecting a chip updates `task.due_date` and acks the delivery
- Reschedule (desktop): opens the app on the task with the date picker focused
- Done twice in a row (Telegram + desktop) → second is a no-op (idempotency)
- Action POST endpoint requires authenticated session + delivery ownership

## Notes
- "Mark task done from reminder" remains a setting (default off). The Done button on a reminder closes the reminder, not the task, by design — this aligns with PRD principle of calmness vs. punishment.
- Reschedule's chip presets must match the rest of the app's date chips for consistency.
- Depends on rm03 (delivery rows + scheduler), rm04 (Telegram channel), rm05 (desktop channel + deep link), tg07 (action registry).

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (Done / Snooze / Reschedule actions), §4 Product Principles (calmness, recovery framing), §14 ReminderRule.

title: RM-07: Important vs Soft visual treatment + intrusion behavior
description:
## Goal
Apply the Important vs Soft visual treatment and intrusion behavior across both Telegram delivery and desktop notification, per the PRD's calmness principle: Important is visible and persistent; Soft is unobtrusive. Neither hijacks the user's screen.

## Scope
- Centralize importance-based formatting in `server/src/reminders/formatting.ts`:
  - Telegram message templates: Important uses bell + bold; Soft is plain
  - Desktop notification: Important is sticky (stays in tray until acted on); Soft auto-dismisses after 8s
- Desktop in-app surfaces:
  - Home page "Now" card shows a small bell badge if an Important reminder is currently pending (un-acked)
  - Active-reminder bar at the bottom of the app shell when ≥1 Important reminder is pending — collapsible, shows count, click to expand list with the same Done/Snooze/Reschedule actions
- Soft reminders do NOT show in the active-reminder bar; they only fire as a single notification
- Reminder list view in Settings → Reminders: "Pending now" section showing currently-firing reminders with quick actions
- No screen-takeover modal, no system-level always-on-top windows — explicitly forbidden per PRD §4 (calmness, not punishment)
- Theme tokens: `--reminder-important-fg`, `--reminder-soft-fg`, `--reminder-bell` — added to design tokens

## Files
- `server/src/reminders/formatting.ts` (centralized templates; rm04 + rm05 import from here)
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/ActiveRemindersBar.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/reminders/PendingReminderBadge.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/settings/RemindersSettings.tsx` (extend with Pending Now section)
- `desktop/src/renderer/styles/tokens.css` (add reminder tokens)
- Refactor: rm04's telegram channel and rm05's desktop notifier consume `formatting.ts` (NOT inline strings)
- Tests: snapshot tests for templates (Important + Soft for both channels)

## Acceptance
- Important reminder produces bell+bold Telegram message and sticky desktop notification
- Soft reminder produces plain Telegram message and auto-dismissing desktop notification
- Home page bell badge appears only when ≥1 Important reminder is pending; clears when all are acked
- Active-reminder bar appears with correct count when Important reminders are pending; expanded view exposes Done/Snooze/Reschedule
- Soft reminders do not appear in the active-reminder bar
- No code path uses `alwaysOnTop`, `setAlwaysOnTop`, or `kiosk` mode for reminders (lint check or grep verifies)
- Visual snapshot/manual screenshot pass for Home page with and without pending Important reminders

title: RM-08: Reminders lifecycle integration test (virtual clock)
description:
## Goal
Integration test pass for the reminders engine — full lifecycle from rule creation through scheduled dispatch to action handling, on both Telegram and desktop notification channels.

## Scope
- Use the Telegram mock from TG-09 + a desktop notification mock that records `Notification` calls
- Time-control: use a virtual clock (Vitest fake timers or sinon) to advance scheduler ticks without real waits
- Specs:
  1. **Rule creation**: create task with `Important` rule, interval=600s → DB shows ReminderRule + next_due_at
  2. **Telegram dispatch**: linked user, advance clock past next_due_at → mock Telegram captures one `sendMessage` with three inline buttons (Done / Snooze 10m / Reschedule)
  3. **Desktop fallback**: unlinked user, advance clock → desktop notification mock records the call (Telegram mock unchanged)
  4. **Done action**: simulate inline button "done" callback → task status='done', rule deactivated
  5. **Snooze action**: "snooze 10m" callback → next_due_at advanced 10m, rule still active
  6. **Reschedule action**: "reschedule" callback → server emits a follow-up message with date picker; selecting "tomorrow 09:00" updates due_at
  7. **Important vs Soft**: dispatch one of each → assert different message templates (e.g., Soft has no escalation copy, Important repeats per interval)
  8. **Escalation**: Important rule, repeat interval=10m, advance clock 30m without ack → 3 dispatches (idempotent — no dupes within a tick)

## Files
- `server/test/integration/reminders/{rule,telegram-dispatch,desktop-dispatch,done,snooze,reschedule,importance,escalation}.spec.ts`
- `server/test/helpers/virtualClock.ts`
- `desktop/test/integration/notification-mock.ts`

## Acceptance
- All eight specs pass
- Tests complete in under 10s with virtual clock
- No real notification fires during the test run
- Idempotency: replaying a tick doesn't double-send

## Skills
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger` only if this task lands a desktop-notification UI test.** The bulk is server-side virtual-clock + supertest, which doesn't need it.

## Notes

title: Telegram bot: linking, capture, voice, commands, outbound
description:
## Goal
Ship the Telegram bot mobile surface: account linking via one-time code, inbound text/voice → Inbox, voice transcription via cloud API, basic slash commands (/now, /today, /inbox), and outbound message infrastructure for reminders to layer on top of in Epic 4.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 3 (Telegram bot).

## Scope
- Telegram bot app (webhook server) with health check
- /start `<linking-code>` flow: generate one-time code in desktop app → user pastes in bot → server links chat ID to user
- Inbound text message → InboxItem (source = telegram-text)
- Inbound voice note → cloud transcription (Whisper or provider equivalent) → InboxItem (source = telegram-voice); raw audio retained until transcription succeeds, then discarded
- /now: show current focus task + next step
- /today: show today's plan
- /inbox: show inbox count + first few items
- Outbound message infra: send Telegram messages with inline action buttons (foundation for Epic 4)
- Settings → Telegram page: linking UI, status, unlink

## Out of scope
- Reminder scheduling/dispatching (Epic 4)
- Reminder action handlers like Done/Snooze/Reschedule (Epic 4)

## Done when
A user with a Telegram account can link in Settings, send a text or voice note that lands in Inbox, and run /now /today /inbox successfully.

## References
PRD §7 mobile surface, §11 Capture (Telegram), §17 Cloud transcription, §22 Risks (Telegram skew).

title: TG-01: Telegram bot service skeleton (webhook + health + env)
description:
## Goal
Stand up the Telegram bot service skeleton inside the existing Fastify sync server: webhook endpoint, bot client wrapper, env config for `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, and a health probe that confirms `getMe` succeeds. This unblocks every other Telegram task.

## Scope

- Use `grammy` (or `node-telegram-bot-api`) — pick `grammy` for typed updates; document choice in `bot.ts` header
- Webhook route: `POST /telegram/webhook` — verifies Telegram secret-token header (`X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`), delegates to update dispatcher
- `GET /telegram/health` returns `{ ok, botUsername, webhookSet }` — calls `getMe` and `getWebhookInfo`
- Environment vars (added to `server/.env.example`): `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL` (public URL for `setWebhook`)
- CLI helper script `server/scripts/telegram-set-webhook.ts` that calls `setWebhook` with the configured URL + secret
- Update dispatcher stub: receives Update, logs `update_id` + type, returns 200 immediately. Real handlers are added in tg03/tg05/tg06.
- Pino redaction for `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`

## Files
- `server/src/telegram/bot.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/webhook.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/config.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts`

## References
PRD §7 Mobile surface — Telegram bot, §20 Architecture (webhook), §23 step 3.

title: TG-02: Linking flow (one-time code + /start handler + TelegramLink)
description:
## Goal
Implement account linking between desktop and Telegram via a one-time code: desktop generates code → user runs `/start <code>` in bot → server links `chat_id` ↔ `user_id` and persists a `TelegramLink` row.

## Scope
- Server endpoint `POST /telegram/linking/code` (auth required) — creates a `telegram_linking_code` row: 8-char alphanumeric, expires in 15 min, single-use, scoped to a user
- Server endpoint `GET /telegram/linking/status` — returns `{ linked: bool, chatId?, telegramUsername?, linkedAt? }`
- Server endpoint `POST /telegram/linking/unlink` — deletes the `TelegramLink` row
- Bot handler for `/start <code>`:
  - if no code: reply with onboarding text directing to desktop Settings → Telegram
  - if code valid + unused + not expired: create `TelegramLink` row, mark code consumed, reply with success
  - if invalid/expired/used: friendly error message
- Migration: `telegram_links` table (`user_id`, `chat_id` unique, `telegram_username`, `linked_at`) and `telegram_linking_codes` table (`code` unique, `user_id`, `expires_at`, `consumed_at` nullable)
- Rate-limit code generation: max 5 active codes per user
- Audit log entry on link/unlink

## Files
- `server/migrations/00xx_telegram_links.sql`
- `server/src/telegram/linking.ts` (route handlers + service)
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/start.ts` (bot handler)
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts` (route `/start` to handler)
- `server/src/telegram/index.ts` (register linking routes)
- `shared/src/types/telegram.ts` (TelegramLink, LinkingCode types — Zod)

## Acceptance
- Authenticated `POST /telegram/linking/code` returns a fresh code; calling again creates an additional code (capped at 5)
- Sending `/start <validCode>` to the bot creates a `telegram_links` row and replies with success message
- Re-sending the same code returns "code already used"; expired codes return expired error
- `GET /telegram/linking/status` reflects linked state correctly before and after unlink
- A user can only have one active link; re-linking from a different chat replaces the previous link and logs the change
- Integration test simulates the full flow with a mocked bot client

## Notes
- The desktop UI is built in tg08; this task only ships server endpoints + bot handler.
- Codes are case-insensitive on input; stored uppercase.
- Store `chat_id` as `BIGINT` — Telegram chat IDs exceed 32-bit.

## References
PRD §7 Telegram bot (Linking), §14 Data Model (TelegramLink), §23 step 3.

title: TG-03: Inbound text -> InboxItem (source=telegram-text)
description:
## Goal
When a linked Telegram user sends a plain text message to the bot (not a slash command), create an `InboxItem` with `source = 'telegram-text'` belonging to that user, and confirm receipt.

## Scope
- Bot text-message handler: filters out commands (anything starting with `/`)
- Resolve user from `chat_id` via `telegram_links`; if unlinked, reply with prompt to link via desktop Settings
- Create `InboxItem`:
  - `user_id` from link
  - `source = 'telegram-text'`
  - `raw_text` from message
  - `created_at = now()`
  - `external_ref = 'tg:<chat_id>:<message_id>'` for idempotency
- Idempotency: if `external_ref` already exists, do not duplicate; reply with original confirmation
- Reply with a short ack (e.g., "Saved to inbox.") — keep it terse per ADHD principle
- Long messages (> 4000 chars) are truncated and noted in the ack
- Telemetry counter: `telegram_capture_text` (only if telemetry opt-in flag is set)

## Files
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/text.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts` (wire text handler)
- `server/src/inbox/service.ts` (add `createFromTelegram` method, or extend existing create)
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/handlers/text.test.ts`

## Acceptance
- Linked user sending "buy milk" creates one `InboxItem` row with `source='telegram-text'` and gets ack reply
- Re-sending the same `message_id` (simulated via Update replay) does NOT create a duplicate
- Unlinked chat_id receives the link-prompt reply; no inbox row created
- Slash commands are NOT treated as text capture (they pass through to slash-command handlers in tg05/tg06)
- Test coverage: linked happy path, unlinked, idempotency, truncation

## Notes
- Editing a Telegram message (`edited_message`) is out of scope; only `message` updates capture.
- Photos/files/stickers — out of scope; reply with "I only handle text and voice notes for now."
- Voice handled in tg04.

## References
PRD §11 Capture (Telegram), §14 InboxItem, §7 Telegram capture.

title: TG-04: Inbound voice -> cloud transcription -> InboxItem
description:
## Goal
Handle inbound Telegram voice notes: download the audio, transcribe via cloud API (Whisper / equivalent), create an `InboxItem` with `source='telegram-voice'` containing the transcript, and discard the raw audio after success.

## Scope
- Voice-message handler in dispatcher: triggers on `message.voice` updates
- Audio download via Telegram `getFile` API → temp path under `server/tmp/telegram-voice/<update_id>.ogg`
- Transcription adapter `server/src/transcription/`:
  - Interface `TranscriptionProvider { transcribe(buffer, mimeType): Promise<{ text, durationSec }> }`
  - `OpenAIWhisperProvider` (POST to `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, model `whisper-1`)
  - `MockProvider` for tests
  - Provider selected via `TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER` env (default `openai`)
- Server-side API key for transcription (`OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY`) — separate from per-user keys; this is one MVP-acceptable place where the server holds a key
- On success: create `InboxItem` with `source='telegram-voice'`, `raw_text=transcript`, `meta={duration_sec, original_message_id}`; delete the temp audio file
- On failure: reply with friendly error per PRD §13; retain audio in temp for up to 1 hour for one retry, then purge
- Reply ack: "Saved to inbox: <first 80 chars of transcript>…"
- Max audio duration: 5 min — longer voices reply with "Voice note too long; please shorten."

## Files
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/voice.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/index.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/openai.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/mock.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/types.ts`
- `server/.env.example` (append `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY`, `TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER`)
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/handlers/voice.test.ts` (uses MockProvider)

## Acceptance
- Voice message ≤ 5 min from a linked user produces an `InboxItem` with non-empty `raw_text` and the temp audio file is deleted
- Transcription failure produces an error reply matching PRD §13 wording; no `InboxItem` created; audio retained for 1h for retry
- Voice > 5 min replies with the length error and is not transcribed
- Unit tests with `MockProvider` cover happy path, provider error, file-too-large
- Pino logs do not include the transcript content (PII) at info level

## Notes
- Telegram voice notes are OGG/Opus; do NOT transcode unless provider rejects (Whisper accepts OGG).
- Per PRD §17: cloud transcription only; no local STT in MVP.
- `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY` is a project-owned key for MVP simplicity. Per-user-key transcription is out of scope.
- Depends on tg01 (bot skeleton), tg02 (linking), tg03 (InboxItem creation pattern).

## References
PRD §11 Capture (voice), §17 Cloud transcription, §13 Error states (voice transcription failed), §22 Risks.

title: TG-05: /now slash command (current focus + next step)

title: TG-06: /today and /inbox slash commands
description:
## Goal
Implement `/today` and `/inbox` slash commands: `/today` shows today's plan; `/inbox` shows inbox count and the first few items.

## Scope
- `/today` handler:
  - Resolve user → query today's scheduled tasks + events for the user's local date
  - Reply: numbered list (max 10), each line `<HH:mm or '—'> <title>`
  - Empty-state: "Nothing scheduled today. Open Plan on desktop to schedule."

  - Resolve user → count of inbox items + first 5 (most recent)
  - Reply: `Inbox: <N> items` + bulleted preview list (truncated to 80 chars per item)
  - Empty-state: "Inbox is empty."
- Both reuse existing server-side queries from desktop (do not duplicate logic)
- Use user's timezone from `UserSettings`; default to UTC if missing, with a one-line hint to set timezone in Settings
- Both commands registered via `setMyCommands` (extend tg05's commands list)
- Unlinked users get link-prompt reply

## Acceptance
- `/today` returns a non-empty numbered list when the user has scheduled tasks/events; empty-state otherwise
- `/inbox` returns count + preview when inbox has items; empty-state otherwise

title: TG-07: Outbound message infra (action buttons + callback router)
description:
## Goal
Build the outbound message infrastructure: a primitive that sends a Telegram message with inline action buttons and persists `OutboundMessage` records so action callbacks can be routed back to the originating intent. This is the foundation Epic 4 (reminders) layers on top of.

## Scope
- `server/src/telegram/outbound.ts` exposing:
  - `sendMessage(userId, { text, buttons })` — `buttons` is `[{ label, actionId, payload }]`
  - Resolves `chat_id` from `telegram_links`; throws `TelegramNotLinkedError` if no link
  - Builds `inline_keyboard` with `callback_data = "<actionId>:<msgId>"` (Telegram callback_data is 64 bytes — encode minimally; full payload stored in DB)
  - Persists `OutboundMessage` row before sending (id, user_id, chat_id, intent, payload JSON, sent_at, telegram_message_id, status)
- Migration: `outbound_messages` table
- Callback handler in dispatcher: receives `callback_query` updates, parses `<actionId>:<msgId>`, looks up `OutboundMessage`, dispatches to action handler registry, calls `answerCallbackQuery`
- Action handler registry: `registerAction(actionId, handler)` — Epic 4 plugs Done/Snooze/Reschedule into this
- Retry logic: on Telegram 5xx or network error, retry 3x with exponential backoff; on 403 (user blocked bot), mark `status='blocked'` and emit a domain event so reminders engine can fall back to desktop notifications
- Edit message support: `editMessage(outboundMessageId, { text, buttons })` for snooze acknowledgements

## Files
- `server/migrations/00xx_outbound_messages.sql`
- `server/src/telegram/outbound.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/actions.ts` (registry)
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/callback.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts` (wire callback_query)
- `shared/src/types/telegram.ts` (OutboundMessage type)
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/outbound.test.ts`, `callback.test.ts`

## Acceptance
- `sendMessage` to a linked user creates an `outbound_messages` row and the user receives the message with the configured buttons
- `sendMessage` to an unlinked user throws `TelegramNotLinkedError`; no row created
- Pressing a button triggers the registered action handler with the resolved payload
- Telegram 403 marks the row `status='blocked'` and emits the domain event (verified via test spy)
- `editMessage` updates the existing message in place (no new row)
- Retries: simulated 5xx is retried 3x then surfaces a clear error

## Notes
- Action handlers themselves (Done/Snooze/Reschedule) are in Epic 4 (rm04, rm06). This task only ships the substrate.
- `callback_data` is intentionally short — the full payload belongs in `outbound_messages.payload`.
- Domain event for `blocked` status is consumed by Epic 4's dispatcher fallback (rm05).

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (delivery + actions), §7 Telegram bot, §13 Error states (Telegram offline/blocked).

title: TG-08: Settings -> Telegram page (link / status / unlink)

title: TG-09: Telegram bot integration test pass (mocked Telegram + voice)

title: AI v1: BYO-key cloud (Anthropic) - triage cleanup, Make Startable, brain-dump split
description:

Ship the first AI surface: cloud-only via single provider (Anthropic) with BYO API key. Three actions: triage cleanup, "Make Startable" task breakdown, brain-dump splitting. All actions are user-invoked, transparent, and undoable.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 7 (AI v1, cloud-only, single provider).

## Scope

- AI orchestration layer: prompt templates, request/response, error handling, token accounting
