title: AI1-02: AI orchestration layer (provider interface, Anthropic impl, prompts, error categorization)
description:
## Goal
Build the AI orchestration layer in `desktop/src/main/ai/`: a provider-agnostic interface, the Anthropic concrete implementation, prompt templates for the three v1 actions, request/response shapes, and categorized error handling. This is the spine every Epic 7 action calls into.

## Scope
- Provider interface:
  ```ts
  interface AIProvider {
    name: 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'ollama'
    complete(req: AIRequest): Promise<AIResponse>
  }
  ```
- `AIRequest` carries `promptClass` (`'triage_cleanup' | 'make_startable' | 'brain_dump_split'`), structured input, max tokens, timeout
- `AIResponse` carries structured output (zod-validated), token counts, model id, latency ms
- Anthropic implementation: `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, fetches key from secret store on each call, never caches key in renderer-reachable memory
- Prompt templates module with one template per `promptClass` and a single shared system preamble (anti-hallucination rules: be concrete, no invented dates, accept-edit-reject framing)
- Error categorization → typed union:
  - `AIError = { kind: 'auth' } | { kind: 'quota' } | { kind: 'network' } | { kind: 'timeout' } | { kind: 'invalid_response' } | { kind: 'unknown', cause }`
- Single dispatch function `runAI(promptClass, input)` that selects provider (v1: hard-coded Anthropic if mode=Cloud) and returns `Result<AIResponse, AIError>`
- All structured outputs validated with Zod; validation failure → `invalid_response`

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/index.ts` — `runAI` dispatcher
- `desktop/src/main/ai/types.ts` — interfaces, Result, AIError
- `desktop/src/main/ai/providers/anthropic.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/triageCleanup.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/makeStartable.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/brainDumpSplit.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/system.ts` — shared preamble
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/ai.ts` — narrow IPC: `runTriageCleanup`, `runMakeStartable`, `runBrainDumpSplit`
- `desktop/src/preload/ai.ts`
- Unit tests: `desktop/src/main/ai/__tests__/anthropic.test.ts` (with sdk mocked)

## Acceptance
- `runAI('triage_cleanup', {...})` with mocked Anthropic returns a Zod-validated structured suggestion
- Forcing 401 from the mocked SDK yields `AIError { kind: 'auth' }`
- Forcing 429 yields `kind: 'quota'`
- Forcing a 30s hang exceeds timeout and yields `kind: 'timeout'` (configurable, default 20s)
- Forcing malformed JSON yields `kind: 'invalid_response'`
- Renderer cannot import the provider directly; only the IPC channel is reachable

## Notes
- This task does NOT persist suggestions — that's `ai1_suggestion_persistence`.
- This task does NOT render UI — UI tasks consume the IPC.
- Provider interface is generic on purpose so Epic 8's OpenAI + Ollama implementations slot in without refactoring callers.

PRD §6 AI Posture, §17 AI Technical Posture (cloud), §22 Risks (latency, hallucination), §13 (error categories).

## Goal

- `runAI` dispatcher (from `ai1_orchestration`) writes a `pending` row after a successful response and returns the `suggestionId` alongside the suggestion
- All three action UI tasks call `recordOutcome` when the user clicks accept / reject / edit-then-save
- `ownerId` is nullable for not-yet-attached suggestions (e.g., a brain-dump split before items are created)

title: AI1-08: Token accounting + rate-limit handling (estimate, record, throttle, 429 backoff)
description:
## Goal
Track token usage and respect rate limits so the user's BYO Anthropic quota is never silently burned. Show estimated tokens before send for higher-cost actions and aggregate per-day usage in Settings.

## Scope
- Pre-flight estimator: a small token-counting helper (Anthropic's tokenizer or a conservative char/4 fallback) returns `{ inputEstimate, maxOutput }` for any prompt
- Brain-dump split modal shows "~X input tokens" before the user confirms (highest input variability)
- On every `runAI` response, persist `{ ts, promptClass, inputTokens, outputTokens, model }` to a new `ai_usage` table (or extend `ai_suggestions`)
- Settings → AI page surfaces a "Today's usage" panel: total requests, input tokens, output tokens, broken down by `promptClass`
- Soft client-side rate limiter: if more than N requests in M seconds across the app, queue with a small "AI is catching up…" indicator (configurable defaults: 5 req / 10 s)
- Honors Anthropic 429: on `quota` error, suspend further AI calls for 60s with a banner

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/usage.ts` — estimator + recorder + reader
- `desktop/src/main/ai/rateLimiter.ts` — simple token-bucket
- `desktop/src/main/ai/index.ts` — wire usage recorder + rate limiter into `runAI`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00XX_ai_usage.sql` — `ai_usage(id, user_id, ts, prompt_class, input_tokens, output_tokens, model)`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/settings/AIUsagePanel.tsx`
- Unit tests: `desktop/src/main/ai/__tests__/rateLimiter.test.ts`, `usage.test.ts`

## Acceptance
- After 3 successful runs, `ai_usage` has 3 rows with non-zero token counts
- Settings panel renders today's totals; restarting the app preserves them
- Bursting 10 calls in 1s causes calls 6-10 to queue (verified by timestamps)
- Quota error suspends new calls for 60s; existing UI shows the banner; deterministic flows remain usable
- Brain-dump modal shows an estimate within ±20% of the actual `input_tokens` recorded post-call

## Notes
- This is the chokepoint that protects user money — keep it simple but always-on.
- Do not bundle a heavyweight tokenizer; the char/4 fallback is acceptable for v1.
- Numbers are local-only; never sent to the sync server (PRD §18: opt-in telemetry, key content never sent).

## References
PRD §17 (BYO key, no server-side proxy), §22 (latency, quota), §13 (quota exceeded), §18 telemetry boundaries.

title: Search: SQLite FTS5 across tasks, inbox, notes
description:
## Goal
Ship a fast keyboard-first full-text search overlay covering tasks, inbox items, and task notes, backed by SQLite FTS5 in the local cache.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 6 (Search).

## Scope
- FTS5 virtual tables for Task title/notes, InboxItem text
- Triggers/handlers to keep FTS in sync on insert/update/delete
- Cmd/Ctrl+K overlay: input, debounced query, ranked result list, keyboard navigation, jump-to-detail
- Result snippeting + highlighting

## Out of scope
- Searching calendar events (calendar is read-only & ephemeral)
- Cross-device search aggregation (local cache only at MVP)

## Done when
Pressing Cmd/Ctrl+K from any screen surfaces a search overlay that returns matching tasks/inbox items/notes within ~50ms on a 10k-item dataset.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §7 desktop item 10, §20 Architecture (local cache).

title: SRCH-01: FTS5 virtual tables + triggers for tasks/inbox/notes (extends F-04)
description:
## Goal
Create FTS5 virtual tables and triggers in the local SQLite cache so tasks, inbox items, and task notes stay fully indexed in real time on insert/update/delete.

## Scope
- Migration extending the F-04 pattern: `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_search_fts.sql`
- Three FTS5 contentless tables (or `content=` external-content) covering:
  - `task_fts(title, notes, content='task', content_rowid='rowid')`
  - `inbox_fts(text, content='inbox_item', content_rowid='rowid')`
  - Tokenizer: `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2 tokenchars '_-'`
- Triggers on each base table (`AFTER INSERT`, `AFTER UPDATE`, `AFTER DELETE`) that mirror changes into the matching FTS table
- For external-content tables, use `INSERT INTO <fts>(<fts>, rowid, ...) VALUES('delete', old.rowid, ...)` pattern on update/delete
- Wrap insert/update/delete on base tables in transactions so FTS stays consistent
- Typed query helper in `desktop/src/main/search/index.ts`: `searchTasks(q, limit)`, `searchInbox(q, limit)`, `searchAll(q, limit)` returning rowids + ranks
- BM25 ranking via FTS5 `bm25()` function with weight tuning: title weighted 2x notes
- Sanitize FTS5 query syntax: escape user input quotes, append `*` to last token for prefix matching

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_search_fts.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/search/index.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/search/query.ts` — query sanitizer + ranker
- `shared/src/types/search.ts` — `SearchHit { id, kind, score, snippet? }`

## Acceptance
- Inserting a task with title `"Pay phone bill"` makes `searchTasks('phone')` return that task
- Updating the task title to `"Renew passport"` makes the old query return zero, new query return the task
- Deleting the task removes it from `searchTasks` results
- A query for `pho` (prefix) finds `phone`
- Diacritic-insensitive: query `cafe` finds title `café`
- BM25 ranks title hits above notes-only hits
- Triggers do not fire infinite loops; bulk-insert of 1k tasks completes in under 2s

## Notes
- Backfill of existing rows is srch-backfill — this task only handles forward-going changes via triggers.
- Calendar events are NOT indexed (PRD §11 scope: tasks, inbox, notes).
- AISuggestion content is NOT indexed.
- Use `external content` tables to avoid duplicating row text on disk.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §20 Architecture (local cache + FTS5), §7 desktop item 10.

title: SRCH-02: Backfill existing rows into FTS on first run after upgrade
description:
## Goal
Backfill the FTS index with existing rows on first run after the search migration is applied so users with pre-existing data get search immediately, not only for newly written rows.

## Scope
- Idempotent backfill job triggered once per FTS-related migration version
- Runs after migrations during app boot (main process), but yields to the UI: chunked in batches of 500 rows with `setImmediate` between batches so app startup is not blocked
- Marker stored in `_meta` (or new `_search_meta` table) keyed by FTS migration version: `{version, status, started_at, finished_at, row_count}`
- Status states: `pending` → `running` → `done` (or `error`); on `done` the job is skipped on subsequent boots
- A "Reindex search" button in Settings → Data resets the marker and re-runs the backfill (manual recovery)
- Logs progress to structured logger (F-13) at debug level: every 5k rows
- Concurrency-safe: only one backfill instance per process; if a write happens during backfill, it's safe because triggers are already firing for new writes

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/search/backfill.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_search_meta.sql` — `_search_meta(version INTEGER PK, status TEXT, ...)`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Data.tsx` — extend with "Reindex search" button (route placeholder exists from F-06)
- Boot wiring in `desktop/src/main/index.ts` to invoke after migrations

## Acceptance
- First boot after migration with 1k existing tasks + 200 inbox items: all rows are searchable within ~2s of UI being ready, without freezing the renderer
- Second boot does not re-run the backfill (marker is `done`)
- "Reindex search" button completes successfully and re-populates FTS even if base tables were never modified
- Killing the process mid-backfill leaves the marker in `running`; on next boot the job re-starts from row 0 (or resumes — implementation choice; document it)
- An empty database completes backfill instantly with `row_count=0` and `status=done`

## Notes
- Do NOT run backfill on every boot — gate by FTS migration version.
- Reindex button is intentionally low-prominence; this is recovery, not a normal flow.
- Performance test for the 10k dataset is srch-perf-test, not this task.

## References
PRD §11, §20 Architecture, §13 (data integrity recovery).

title: SRCH-03: Search overlay UI (debounced input, ranked list, keyboard nav)
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 search overlay placeholder with a real keyboard-first overlay: debounced input, ranked result list, keyboard navigation, and jump-to-detail.

## Scope
- Trigger: Cmd/Ctrl+K from any route opens overlay (already wired in F-06; keep the binding)
- Modal layer: full-screen blur backdrop, centered card; Esc closes; Esc in input also closes (not just clears)
- Input: autofocus on open; debounced 120ms; clears on close
- Result list: max 30 results across all kinds (tasks, inbox, notes-on-tasks); grouped by kind with section headers
- Keyboard nav: ↑/↓ moves selection (wraps at edges), Enter jumps to detail route, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter opens in new context if applicable, Tab cycles section
- Jump-to-detail:
  - Task hit → navigate to `/inbox` or `/plan` and focus that task (use a `pendingFocusId` query param or store)
  - Inbox hit → navigate to `/inbox` and focus item
- Empty state: "Type to search your tasks, inbox, and notes." (no results yet)
- No-results state: "No matches for `<q>`."
- Loading: search calls run in main process via IPC; show subtle spinner only if >150ms
- Overlay state lives outside route tree (singleton) so it can open from anywhere

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/SearchOverlay.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/search/ResultRow.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/state/searchStore.ts` — open/close, query, results
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/search.ts` — `search(query, limit)` handler
- `desktop/src/preload/search.ts` — `search.query(q)`

## Acceptance
- Cmd/Ctrl+K opens overlay; Esc closes
- Typing "phone" within 200ms (after debounce) populates results from a seeded DB
- ↑/↓ moves selection visually; Enter routes to the correct detail and the target item is visually focused
- Clicking outside the card closes the overlay
- Re-opening preserves no prior input (clean slate)
- No layout shift on the underlying page when overlay opens

## Notes
- Snippeting + highlighting is srch-snippet — show plain titles for now, but make the row component accept an optional snippet prop.
- Performance budget verification is srch-perf-test.
- Calendar events are NOT searchable.
- Do NOT implement saved searches, search history, or filters — out of MVP scope.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §7 desktop item 10, §10 (keyboard-first).

title: SRCH-04: Snippeting + highlighting in result rows
description:
## Goal
Render snippeted, highlighted match context in result rows so users can see why a hit matched without opening the detail.

## Scope
- Use FTS5 `snippet()` function in the search query: `snippet(<fts>, <colidx>, '<mark>', '</mark>', '...', 16)` returning ~16 tokens around the match
- For task hits: prefer snippet from `notes` if the title hit is exact; if title was the match, show full title with highlight; if both match, show title + brief notes snippet
- Inbox hits: snippet from `text`
- Renderer renders `<mark>` segments with a highlight style (no bg color, just bold/underline to keep visual calm)
- Sanitize: snippet output is mostly safe but treat as untrusted; render via a tokenizer that splits on `<mark>` / `</mark>` and creates React fragments — DO NOT use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
- Long titles are truncated with ellipsis past 80 chars; snippet stays around 120 chars

## Files
- Extend `desktop/src/main/search/index.ts` to return `{ id, kind, score, titleHtml, snippetHtml }` (where `*Html` is actually a structured array of `{ text, highlighted }` segments — name `titleSegments`/`snippetSegments`)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/search/Highlight.tsx` — segment renderer
- Update `desktop/src/renderer/components/search/ResultRow.tsx` to consume segments
- `shared/src/types/search.ts` — extend `SearchHit` with segments

## Acceptance
- Searching `phone` against a task with notes "remember to pay phone bill before friday" returns a snippet like `…remember to pay <mark>phone</mark> bill before friday…`
- Highlighted segments render bolded (or per chosen style); no raw `<mark>` tags appear in the DOM as text
- A query with no notes and a title hit shows the title with the matched word highlighted
- Snippet length stays within bounds; no layout overflow in the overlay
- Special characters in user content (`<`, `&`, etc.) render as literal text, not HTML

## Notes
- Highlight style intentionally calm per PRD voice — avoid yellow background; use weight or underline.
- Multi-word queries: FTS5 `snippet()` already handles multiple matches; just pass through.
- Do NOT use a JS-side highlighter library — the FTS5 snippet output is sufficient.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §10 (calm voice).

title: SRCH-05: Search performance test (10k rows, p95 < 50ms)
description:
## Goal
Add an automated performance test that verifies search returns results within the PRD budget (~50ms p95) on a 10k-row dataset.

## Scope
- Test harness lives under `desktop/test/perf/search.perf.test.ts` (vitest or node:test — match repo's existing runner)
- Dataset generator: seeds an isolated SQLite DB with 8k tasks (varied title/notes, ~30 tokens avg) + 2k inbox items; deterministic seed for reproducibility
- Runs the FTS index/backfill once; then executes 100 randomized queries (mix of single-token, two-token, prefix queries)
- Records latency per query; asserts p50 < 20ms and p95 < 50ms on a baseline machine; logs full distribution for debugging
- The test is opt-in (skipped by default in normal CI) but runnable via `pnpm --filter desktop test:perf`
- A single CI workflow `perf-search.yml` runs it on push to main and posts a summary to the run log; threshold failure does NOT block PRs (advisory) but DOES fail the workflow status

## Files
- `desktop/test/perf/search.perf.test.ts`
- `desktop/test/perf/seed.ts` — dataset generator
- `desktop/package.json` — add `test:perf` script
- `.github/workflows/perf-search.yml` — opt-in CI job

## Acceptance
- `pnpm --filter desktop test:perf` runs locally and prints a latency report
- p95 latency is under 50ms on a standard dev machine; if not, the test fails with a clear message including the actual p50/p95
- Test isolates its DB to a temp path; does not pollute the user's dev DB
- Re-running with the same seed produces identical row counts (seed determinism)
- Skipped during normal `pnpm test` runs (marked or guarded by env var)

## Notes
- Calibration: thresholds may need tuning per machine class. If CI hardware is slow, adjust the workflow threshold but keep local dev threshold at 50ms.
- Do NOT include this test in the default test suite — it's slow and noisy.
- This test depends on srch-fts-tables and srch-backfill being merged.

## References
PRD §11 Search ("ranked, fast results"), PRD acceptance for fast search; rule of thumb 50ms p95.

title: SRCH-06: FTS5 accuracy + ranking test pass
description:
## Goal
FTS5 accuracy test pass — verify search relevance, ranking, and snippeting against a curated query/expected-result corpus. Complements the perf test in SRCH-05.

## Scope
- Curated dataset: 200 InboxItems + 200 Tasks + 100 Notes covering common ADHD-flavored content (e.g., "buy milk", "pay car rego", "draft Q3 review", "kid's permission slip Tuesday")
- 30 queries with expected top-3 result sets (golden file `desktop/test/fixtures/search/golden.json`)
- Specs (Vitest):
  1. **Exact match**: query "permission slip" returns the permission-slip task in position 1
  2. **Stemming**: query "draft" returns "drafting" / "drafts" hits
  3. **Multi-word**: query "Q3 review" beats unrelated "Q3" or "review" only
  4. **Tokenization**: punctuation stripped (e.g., "kid's" matches "kids")
  5. **Field weighting**: title hits rank above notes hits for same term
  6. **Recency tiebreaker**: among equal-relevance hits, more recent updated_at wins
  7. **Snippet correctness**: returned snippets contain highlighted match terms wrapped in markers
  8. **Empty / very short query**: returns a stable empty result set, not a crash
- Soft regression check: each query's top-3 ordering matches the golden file (allowing per-version golden updates with explicit reviewer sign-off)

## Files
- `desktop/test/integration/search/accuracy.spec.ts`
- `desktop/test/fixtures/search/{corpus.json,golden.json}`

## Acceptance
- All eight spec groups pass
- Golden-file mismatches surface as readable diff, not opaque assertion failure
- Adding a new corpus row doesn't require touching unrelated golden entries

## Skills
None required — this is pure Vitest against the local SQLite cache.

## Notes
- This task complements SRCH-05 (perf test). They run in the same CI job (`e2e-search`).
- Corpus is English-only at MVP; multilingual is out of scope.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §7 desktop item 10.

title: F-05b: DB round-trip integration test for core model (Vitest + better-sqlite3)
description:
## Goal
Add the integration test that round-trips one row of every table in the core model through better-sqlite3, validating both the SQL schema and the Zod parsers.

## Why this is split from F-05
F-05 lands the schema and Zod types and verifies the migration applies cleanly on a fresh DB via the Electron-launch smoke test. The proper DB round-trip test needs Vitest infra (provided by F-03) and a Node-ABI better-sqlite3 build separate from the Electron-ABI one used at runtime. Splitting keeps F-05 a single-iteration P0 deliverable and lets the sonnet worker land this once F-03 ships.

## Scope
- Add Vitest to desktop (or wherever the test lives) once F-03 brings the test runner
- Resolve the Node vs Electron ABI rebuild problem (e.g., separate `pnpm rebuild-native:node` script, or use node:sqlite, or run tests under Electron)
- For each table in `0003_core_model.sql`:
  1. Apply migrations to a fresh in-memory DB
  2. Insert one row constructed via the Zod schema (`Schema.parse(...)`)
  3. SELECT the row back, parse via `Schema.parse(row)`, deep-equal compare
- Verify FK cascade: deleting a user removes their inbox/tasks/events/etc.
- Verify CHECK constraints reject invalid enum values

## Acceptance
- `pnpm -r test` runs and passes the integration suite
- One round-trip assertion per table
- One cascade assertion (delete user → child rows gone)
- One CHECK violation assertion (bad enum rejected by DB)

## References
PRD §14, parent F-05.

title: Telemetry, onboarding polish, empty/error states
description:
## Goal
Ship opt-in telemetry, complete the empty/error state coverage from PRD §13, and harden onboarding so the deferred-integration model from §12 works in practice.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 9.

## Scope
- Opt-in telemetry pipeline (off by default): feature use counts, session length, AI accept/reject/edit rates, error types — never task content
- Opt-in crash reporting (separate toggle)
- "What is sent" inspector: user can view exact telemetry payload before sending
- Empty states from PRD §13: first open, empty inbox, nothing scheduled, no current focus, review with no completed
- Error states from PRD §13: calendar fail, OAuth expired, Telegram offline / blocked, voice transcription failed, Telegram not linked when expected, sync failed, Ollama not running, key missing/invalid, API failed/timeout, quota exceeded
- Each state: tells user what happened, what to do, whether anything is lost
- Onboarding: 5-min first-run requires only magic-link sign-in; integrations deferred to moment-of-need
- Keyboard shortcuts pass: Cmd/Ctrl+K search, capture hotkey, focus controls, navigation

## Done when
Each integration / failure mode has a tested user-facing state, telemetry can be enabled/inspected/disabled, and a new user can complete first-run in under 5 minutes without configuring any integration.

## References
PRD §12 Onboarding, §13 Empty/Error States, §18 Telemetry.

title: POL-01: Telemetry pipeline (opt-in, allow-listed events, client batching + server ingest)
description:
## Goal
Ship the opt-in telemetry pipeline (off by default) — desktop client batching of allow-listed events and a server ingestion endpoint — so adoption / friction signals can be measured without ever capturing task, calendar, Telegram, or API-key content.

## Scope
- Allow-list of event names (e.g., `app.opened`, `capture.created`, `triage.completed`, `ai.suggestion.accepted|rejected|edited`, `error.shown`) — defined in `shared/src/telemetry/events.ts`
- Strict prop allow-list per event: only booleans, ints, short enum strings, and stable IDs (`anonymous_id`, `session_id`); no free text, no titles, no message bodies
- Client batcher: buffers events in SQLite (`telemetry_outbox` table), flushes every 60s or 50 events when telemetry is enabled; drops silently when disabled
- Anonymous device ID generated on first run (UUID v4), stored in secret store; never tied to user account
- Server endpoint: `POST /telemetry/ingest` accepts batched payloads, validates against the same allow-list, writes to `telemetry_events` table; rejects with 400 on unknown event/prop
- Hard kill switch: setting `telemetry.enabled = false` immediately stops emission AND purges outbox
- Reuse `logger.event` allow-list helper from F-13 as the single emission API

## Files
- `shared/src/telemetry/events.ts` (event + prop schema, Zod)
- `shared/src/telemetry/client.ts` (batcher, flush, allow-list enforcement)
- `desktop/src/main/telemetry/index.ts` (SQLite outbox + flush worker)
- `desktop/migrations/00XX_telemetry_outbox.sql`
- `server/src/routes/telemetry.ts` (ingest endpoint)
- `server/migrations/00XX_telemetry_events.sql`

## Acceptance
- With telemetry off (default), zero network calls to `/telemetry/ingest`; outbox stays empty
- With telemetry on, batched events arrive at server within 60s; payloads strictly schema-validated
- Attempting to emit an unknown event name throws in tests; attempting to attach a non-allow-listed prop throws
- Disabling telemetry mid-session purges outbox and stops further sends
- Server rejects payloads containing fields like `title`, `body`, `message` with 400

## Notes
- This task is the pipeline only; the Settings UI (toggle + inspector) is a separate task (`pol_telemetry_ui`).
- Crash reporting is a separate, independent toggle (`pol_crash_reporting`).
- Keep the anonymous_id rotation policy documented but not user-facing in MVP.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry (opt-in, captures listed; never captures task/calendar/Telegram content/API keys), §23 step 9, §4 (Trustworthy, transparent).

title: POL-10: Visual regression + a11y + anti-shame copy audit
description:
## Goal
Visual regression and accessibility audit pass — Playwright visual snapshots of every primary screen + axe-core a11y sweep. Locks the design language in place and surfaces accessibility regressions.

## Scope
- **Visual regression**:
  - Playwright `toHaveScreenshot()` snapshots of: Home (empty + populated), Inbox (focused triage), Plan (with events + tasks), Focus (active session + idle), Review (with completed items), Settings (each sub-page), Sign-in
  - Light + dark theme variants (if dark theme implemented; else single mode)
  - Snapshots stored under `desktop/e2e/visual/__snapshots__/`
  - Update flow: `pnpm test:visual --update-snapshots` for intentional changes
- **Accessibility audit**:
  - `@axe-core/playwright` integration; one check per primary screen
  - Zero violations of `wcag2a` and `wcag2aa` rules
  - Manual a11y checklist (in this task's PR description): keyboard-only walkthrough, focus order, screen-reader names for icons
- **Anti-shame language audit**: programmatic check that copy strings on error/empty/recovery screens do NOT contain banned words from `desktop/src/copy/banned.ts` (e.g., "failed", "you should have", "missed", "wasted") — replace with PRD §4 anti-shame alternatives

## Files
- `desktop/e2e/visual/{home,inbox,plan,focus,review,settings,signin}.visual.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/a11y/all-screens.spec.ts`
- `desktop/test/copy/banned-words.spec.ts`
- `desktop/src/copy/banned.ts` — list of banned words + suggested replacements

## Acceptance
- Visual snapshots committed; CI fails on diffs
- Zero axe wcag2aa violations across all primary screens
- No banned words in any user-facing string (test scrapes the bundled renderer for known copy keys)
- Manual checklist completed and recorded in the PR

## Skills
**Invoke `frontend-design`** to review the snapshots and inform per-screen visual decisions before locking them in. The skill helps avoid the generic-AI-aesthetic trap and aligns with PRD §4 design principles.
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger`** for the Playwright visual + a11y harness — flake-resistant snapshot configuration in Electron is non-trivial.

## Notes
- Snapshots are notoriously flaky on different render backends — pin the CI runner to a fixed image and run with `--reporter=line`.
- This task is the design-quality gate before MVP ship.

## References
PRD §4 Product Principles, §13 Empty/Error states (anti-shame language).
notes:
## UI design reference
Use `GUI_draft.ts` (repo root) as the visual + interaction reference for this task. It establishes the palette (stone + emerald), shapes (soft rounded — `rounded-[1.8rem]`, `rounded-[2.5rem]`), typography (serif italic hero headers, sans body), iconography (lucide-react + custom MountainClimberIcon), kanban-column layout for Inbox/Today/This Week, drag-and-drop affordances, and motion (fade-in / slide-in). Reuse its Tailwind class patterns unless there is a clear reason to deviate. Pair with the `frontend-design` skill after loading the draft.

title: POL-02: Telemetry settings UI — toggle + 'what is sent' inspector
description:
## Goal
Build the Settings UI for telemetry — a clear opt-in toggle, a "what is sent" inspector showing the exact payload of buffered events, and the ability to opt out at any time — so users can verify the privacy claim themselves.

## Scope
- Settings → Privacy → Telemetry section
- Toggle: "Help improve Calmly with anonymous usage data" — off by default; copy explains what is + isn't sent in plain language
- "What is sent" inspector: live view of the most recent N (e.g., 50) events currently buffered in the outbox, with raw JSON expandable per event
- Inspector also shows the static allow-list (event names + accepted props) so power users can audit what's possible to send
- "Send a test event now" button (dev/QA aid; gated to non-prod or always-on but harmless)
- Disabling the toggle immediately calls the purge hook from `pol_telemetry_pipeline`
- Link to the public docs page describing the telemetry endpoint (placeholder URL is fine)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/TelemetrySection.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/TelemetryInspector.tsx`
- `desktop/src/preload/telemetry.ts` (narrow IPC: `getOutbox`, `getAllowList`, `setEnabled`, `purge`)
- Settings copy in `shared/src/copy/settings.ts`

## Acceptance
- Toggling off purges outbox and stops emission (verified in e2e test)
- Inspector shows real buffered events when telemetry is on; shows empty state with allow-list reference when off
- Copy passes the anti-shame / transparency review: no dark-pattern phrasing, default state is clearly OFF
- Keyboard-accessible: tab order, screen-reader labels on toggle and JSON disclosure controls

## Notes
- Depends on `pol_telemetry_pipeline` for the outbox + purge primitives.
- This is intentionally separate from crash reporting — different toggle, different copy.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry ("users can inspect what is sent"), §4 (Trustworthy, Anti-shame), §23 step 9.

title: POL-03: Crash reporting (Electron crashReporter, opt-in, separate toggle)
description:
## Goal
Ship opt-in Electron crash reporting as a toggle separate from telemetry, so users can choose to share native crashes (main + renderer) without enabling usage telemetry.

## Scope
- Activate Electron `crashReporter` (configured during F-13 with `uploadToServer: false`); flipping the Settings toggle enables `submitURL` and uploads
- Server endpoint: `POST /crash/ingest` accepts minidump uploads (multipart/form-data); stores blob + metadata to disk or object storage path; no user content beyond stack
- Strip identifiers: no email, no anonymous_id correlation with telemetry events; just `app_version`, `os`, `process_type`
- Settings → Privacy → Crash Reports section: independent toggle with copy explaining what's in a crash report and what isn't
- "View last crash report" button if a dump exists locally (read-only inspector listing file size, timestamp, version)
- Toggle change requires restart to take effect — surface a clear non-modal banner saying "Restart Calmly to apply"
- Default OFF on every fresh install and after migration

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/crash/index.ts` (configure crashReporter, handle restart-required state)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/CrashReportSection.tsx`
- `server/src/routes/crash.ts`
- `desktop/src/preload/crash.ts` (narrow IPC: `getStatus`, `setEnabled`, `getLastReportMeta`)

## Acceptance
- Default OFF; toggling ON + restart begins uploading on next crash
- Toggling OFF prevents any upload after next start; in-flight queued dumps are deleted from local cache
- Crash payload contains no email, no task content, no API keys (verified by test that triggers a renderer crash and inspects the captured file)
- Server endpoint accepts a dump and returns 202; rejects oversized payloads (>10 MB) with 413

## Notes
- Symbol upload + symbolication is out of scope for this task; raw dumps are enough for MVP.
- Settings UI lives next to the telemetry section but the toggles are wholly independent.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry ("crash reports are separate and also opt-in"), §4 (Trustworthy), §23 step 9.

title: POL-04: Error states pass — calendar, OAuth, Telegram, voice transcription, sync (shared <ErrorState>)
description:
## Goal
Implement consistent, recovery-oriented error states for all integration failures from PRD §13 — calendar fail, OAuth expired, Telegram offline / blocked / not linked, voice transcription failed, sync failed — backed by a shared `<ErrorState>` component so every state answers: what happened, what to do, whether anything is lost.

## Scope
- Build `<ErrorState>` component: icon, headline, body copy, primary action button, optional secondary "learn more" link, optional "loss disclosure" line ("Nothing is lost — your captures are safe locally")
- Variants per integration failure with concrete copy + recovery action:
  - Calendar connection failed (Google or Microsoft) → "Reconnect"
  - Calendar OAuth token expired → "Sign in again"
  - Telegram offline (delivery failed network) → "Retry now"; auto-retry with backoff in background
  - Telegram bot blocked / user removed bot → "Re-link Telegram" with link flow entry point

title: Calendar integration: Google + Microsoft 365 read-only import
description:
## Goal
Read-only import of external calendars so committed events appear in Plan and the user can plan around them. Google Calendar first, Microsoft 365 second.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 5 (Calendar). PRD says Google first, then Microsoft — file dependency in this order.

## Scope
- Google Calendar OAuth flow (server-side proxy for callback) + refresh-token storage encrypted on client
- Microsoft 365 Calendar OAuth flow + refresh-token storage encrypted on client
- Periodic + on-demand import worker → CalendarEventImport rows
- Display imported events in Plan view alongside user-scheduled tasks
- Token-expiry handling with re-auth prompt
- Settings → Calendar page: connect / disconnect / status per provider

## Out of scope (PRD §15)
- Creating events in external calendars
- Two-way sync
- Apple Calendar / iCloud / CalDAV

## Done when
A user can connect Google (and Microsoft) calendars, see their events in Plan, and re-auth gracefully when tokens expire.

## References
PRD §15 Calendar Integration, §22 risks (OAuth edge cases, timezones, recurrence).

title: CAL-01: Google Calendar OAuth flow (server callback proxy + scopes + refresh token)
description:
## Goal
Implement the end-to-end Google Calendar OAuth flow so a user can connect their Google account from the desktop client and the server captures a refresh token via a callback proxy.

## Scope
- Server-side OAuth callback proxy on the sync server: `GET /oauth/google/start`, `GET /oauth/google/callback`
- Scopes: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly`, `openid`, `email`, `profile`
- PKCE + `state` (CSRF) parameters with state tied to authenticated user session
- Exchange code for tokens server-side; capture `refresh_token` (force `access_type=offline&prompt=consent` to ensure issuance)
- Hand refresh token + access token + expiry back to the client over an authenticated channel (signed short-lived bundle the client redeems via `POST /oauth/google/redeem`)
- Client-side trigger: open external browser to start URL, listen for `calmly://oauth/google/done?ticket=...` deep-link, redeem ticket, persist via F-12 secret store (real persistence in cal-2)
- Connection metadata row: `CalendarAccount(provider='google', external_account_id, email, status)`

## Files
- `server/src/routes/oauth/google.ts` — start, callback, redeem
- `server/src/services/googleOAuth.ts` — token exchange + ticket signing
- `server/src/db/migrations/00xx_calendar_account.sql` — accounts table
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/googleOAuth.ts` — open browser, deep-link handler, redeem ticket
- `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` — `calendar.connectGoogle()` (returns connection status)
- `shared/src/types/calendar.ts` — `CalendarAccount`, `OAuthRedeemTicket`

## Acceptance
- A user clicks "Connect Google" in Settings → Calendar (placeholder UI ok), browser opens, user consents, deep-link returns to app, refresh token is persisted via F-12, `CalendarAccount` row exists with `status='connected'`
- `state` mismatch or expired ticket returns clear error and does not persist
- Refresh token is never logged or sent to telemetry
- Forcing the consent flow guarantees `refresh_token` is present even on re-connect

## Notes
- Token storage uses the secret-store key `calendar.google.refresh_token:<account_id>` defined in F-12 — DO NOT invent a new keychain.
- Microsoft 365 lives in cal-ms-oauth and mirrors this structure.
- Display UI polish (cards, status pills, last-sync) is in cal-settings-page; this task only needs a minimal entry point.

## References
PRD §15 Calendar Integration, §22 risks (calendar OAuth edge cases), §14 (encrypted at rest).

title: CAL-02: Microsoft 365 Calendar OAuth flow (parallel to Google)
description:
## Goal
Implement the Microsoft 365 Calendar OAuth flow in parallel structure to Google, so a user can connect a work/personal MS account and the server captures a refresh token.

## Scope
- Server-side proxy: `GET /oauth/microsoft/start`, `GET /oauth/microsoft/callback`, `POST /oauth/microsoft/redeem`
- Authority: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0` (multi-tenant; supports work + personal)
- Scopes: `offline_access`, `Calendars.Read`, `User.Read`, `openid`, `profile`, `email`
- PKCE + `state` (CSRF) bound to user session
- Exchange code for tokens server-side; capture `refresh_token` (requires `offline_access` scope)
- Same signed-ticket redemption pattern as Google so client never sees the auth code
- Persist refresh token via F-12 secret store under `calendar.microsoft.refresh_token:<account_id>`
- `CalendarAccount(provider='microsoft', ...)` row

## Files
- `server/src/routes/oauth/microsoft.ts`
- `server/src/services/microsoftOAuth.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/microsoftOAuth.ts`
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` with `calendar.connectMicrosoft()`
- Reuse `shared/src/types/calendar.ts`

## Acceptance
- Clicking "Connect Microsoft" in Settings → Calendar opens browser, completes consent, deep-links back, refresh token persists, `CalendarAccount(provider='microsoft')` exists with `status='connected'`
- Both work (Azure AD) and personal (MSA) accounts complete the flow against the `/common` authority
- State mismatch / expired ticket rejected with clear error

## Notes
- Reuse the ticket-signing helper from cal-google-oauth — do not re-invent it. If you need to refactor it into a shared service in `server/src/services/oauthTickets.ts`, do so.

title: CAL-03: Encrypted refresh-token storage + access-token refresh (uses F-12 secret store)
description:
## Goal
Wire calendar refresh-token persistence and retrieval through the F-12 secret store so OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest and only the main process can use them.

## Scope
- Typed accessor module: `calendarTokens.set(provider, accountId, refreshToken)`, `.get(provider, accountId)`, `.delete(provider, accountId)`
- Backed by F-12 `secretStore` with namespaced keys `calendar.<provider>.refresh_token:<account_id>`
- Access-token cache (in-memory, never written to disk) with expiry timestamp; a `getAccessToken(provider, accountId)` helper that refreshes via the provider's token endpoint when expired
- Refresh failures (revoked, invalid_grant) mark the `CalendarAccount.status = 'reauth_required'` and surface an event the renderer can subscribe to
- IPC: renderer can call `calendar.disconnect(accountId)` which clears the secret AND the account row

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/tokens.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/refresh.ts` — provider-agnostic refresh dispatcher
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/google.ts`, `providers/microsoft.ts` — refresh endpoints + scopes
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` with `disconnect`, `listAccounts`, `onAccountStatusChanged`

## Acceptance
- Stored refresh tokens roundtrip through encrypted storage (DB inspection shows ciphertext)
- Calling `getAccessToken` when access token is fresh returns from cache without network
- When access token is expired, refresh is called and a new access token is cached
- Revoking the token externally → next refresh returns `invalid_grant` → `CalendarAccount.status = 'reauth_required'` and renderer receives event
- `disconnect(accountId)` removes the secret AND the account row; subsequent `listAccounts` does not include it

## Notes
- DO NOT expose access tokens or refresh tokens to the renderer over IPC — only status booleans and identifiers.
- This task assumes cal-google-oauth and cal-ms-oauth have already populated the secret store on first connect; this task generalizes the read/refresh path.
- Backoff on refresh failures: exponential, capped at 5 min, halt after 5 consecutive failures and mark `reauth_required`.

## References
PRD §14 (API keys / tokens encrypted at rest), §15, §22 risks (token expiry).

title: CAL-04: Calendar import worker (periodic + on-demand, recurrence + timezones)
description:
## Goal
Implement a calendar import worker that fetches events from each connected provider on a schedule (and on demand), expands recurrences, normalizes timezones, and writes `CalendarEventImport` rows to the local cache.

## Scope
- Periodic worker in main process: every 15 min while app is running, and on-demand via `calendar.refresh(accountId?)` IPC
- Window: from `now() - 1d` to `now() + 30d` (sliding); incremental sync uses provider sync tokens where available (Google `syncToken`, Microsoft `deltaLink`)
- Recurrence: request server-expanded instances where supported (Google `singleEvents=true&timeMin=&timeMax=`, Microsoft `calendarView` endpoint) so we never expand RRULE locally
- Timezones: store all times as UTC `INTEGER` epoch ms in DB, plus original timezone string for display; convert to user's local TZ in the renderer
- Event de-duplication by `(provider, account_id, external_id)`; updates use `recurringEventId + originalStartTime` for instance-level identity
- Cancellations: provider returns `status='cancelled'` → soft-delete the row (or hard delete after 24h)
- Migration: `CalendarEventImport(id, account_id, provider, external_id, recurring_event_id, title, location, start_utc, end_utc, all_day, tz, status, etag, updated_at)` with index on `(account_id, start_utc)`
- Concurrency: only one import per account at a time; queue further requests

## Files

title: CAL-06: Token-expiry handling + re-auth prompt
description:
## Goal
Detect expired or revoked calendar OAuth tokens, surface a clear re-auth prompt to the user, and complete the re-auth flow without losing imported event history or requiring full disconnect.

## Scope

- Reconnect button starts the same OAuth start flow as initial connect, but reuses the existing `CalendarAccount` row (matches by `external_account_id` + provider) instead of creating a new one
- On successful re-auth, status flips back to `connected`; `lastSyncAt` is preserved; import worker resumes on next tick
- Events imported before re-auth are NOT deleted; only stale events older than the import window are pruned naturally
- Tested error paths: user denies consent on re-auth, user picks a different account on re-auth (treat as new account, do not silently rebind)

title: Deterministic core loop: Capture to Review (no AI/Telegram/calendar)
description:
## Goal
Ship the deterministic (no-AI, no-Telegram, no-calendar) full daily loop: a user can capture an item, triage it, plan their day, focus on a task, replan when off-track, and complete daily shutdown — all from the desktop app.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 2 (Deterministic core loop).

## Scope
- Home screen: Now, Next, Today; persistent capture bar; conditional Inbox/Triage card; Replan + Quick Plan entry points
- Capture: quick-add UI + global hotkey; persists to InboxItem
- Inbox / Triage: one-item-at-a-time UI; classify type, due-date chips, route to Today/This Week/Later; inline "break it down"; snooze/skip
- Plan: day view with manual time blocks (no calendar import yet), drag/drop reorder, simple reschedule

- AI suggestions of any kind (Epics 7–8)
- Calendar import (Epic 5)
- Telegram or any reminders (Epics 3–4)
- Full-text search overlay (Epic 6)

## Done when
All core-loop tasks closed AND a single user can complete the full Capture→Triage→Plan→Focus→Replan→Review loop in one day on desktop with no AI / Telegram / calendar configured.

## References
PRD §5 (Core Value Prop), §7 (MVP Scope desktop), §9 (Core Journey), §11 (Functional Requirements), §13 (Empty/Error States).

title: CL-10: 'I'm stuck' deterministic guided prompts (no AI)
description:
## Goal
Implement the "I'm stuck" guided rescue inside Focus mode using a fixed, deterministic prompt sequence (no AI). One question at a time; the user can answer, skip, or exit at any step.

## Scope
- "I'm stuck" button in CL-FOCUS opens an inline overlay (does not change route)
- Fixed prompt sequence (5 prompts; user can answer in a textarea or skip):
  1. "What's the smallest next thing you could do — even something tiny?"
  2. "Is the task unclear? If so, what's the question?"
  3. "Do you need a person, an answer, or a piece of info?"
  4. "Could a 5-minute version count as done?"
  5. "Can you switch to a different task and return later?"
- One question on screen at a time; **Next** advances; **Back** goes back; **Skip** advances without saving; **End rescue** closes the overlay
- Answers (if any) saved as a single appended note on the current task — append to `tasks.notes` with format `\n\n--- Stuck rescue (ISO timestamp) ---\nQ: ...\nA: ...\n` (one block per session)
- After step 5, show outcome buttons:
  - **Continue current task** → close overlay, return to ActiveSession
  - **Switch task** → opens SwitchTaskPicker (CL-FOCUS)
  - **Take a break** → ends focus session, returns to Home
- Track each rescue session in `stuck_sessions` table (new migration `0008_stuck_sessions.sql`) — id, focus_session_id, started_at, ended_at, outcome enum

## Acceptance

- Filling answers for prompts 1, 3 and skipping 2, 4, 5 then clicking "Continue current task" appends a notes block to the task with only the answered Qs
- Clicking "Switch task" ends the stuck_session with outcome='switch' AND opens the switch picker
- Clicking "Take a break" ends both the stuck_session AND the focus_session
- Unit test: prompts array is the source of truth; verify exactly 5 prompts in correct order
- E2E test: full flow — open, answer one, skip one, end with switch outcome — assert DB rows

## Notes

  - **Reflection** — optional single-line input "One word about today" or longer free-text (max 280 chars); saved to `daily_reflections` table (new migration `0010_daily_reflections.sql`)

- "Skip shutdown" button — closes without writing reflection; does NOT mark last_shutdown_date

title: CL-15: Full daily-loop E2E test pass (Capture → Review)
description:
## Goal
Full daily-loop E2E test pass that exercises the deterministic core loop end-to-end: Capture → Inbox → Triage → Plan → Focus → Replan → Review. This is the MVP gating test for Epic 2 — if this passes, the deterministic shape of the product is provably working.

## Scope
- One Playwright spec `loop.spec.ts` that walks the full happy path:
  1. **Capture**: invoke global hotkey, type "buy birthday card", press Enter — verify InboxItem row created
  2. **Triage**: open `/inbox` triage focused mode → classify as task → set due_at = today → route to "Today" → next item
  3. **Plan**: navigate to `/plan` → drag the new task to the 14:00 slot → assert scheduled_at persisted
  4. **Focus**: from Home, click "Start focus" on the 14:00 task → assert FocusSession row created → click "Mark done" → assert task.status = 'done', session.ended_at set
  5. **Replan**: with one remaining unfinished task, open Replan from Focus → "Push to tomorrow" → assert due_at advanced
  6. **Review**: navigate to `/review` → assert "1 completed today" + "1 unfinished" → carry-forward unfinished → save reflection "long day" → complete shutdown → assert reflection persisted, last_shutdown_date set
- Negative-path mini-specs: capture without title (should reject), triage skip (item stays in inbox), Replan drop (task → status='dropped')
- Empty-state spec: fresh user → Home shows first-open empty state → capture flow still works
- CI integration: `e2e-core-loop` job depends on `e2e-foundations`

title: CL-09: Focus mode — current task + next step, soft time, mark done, switch task
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Focus placeholder with a real focus mode UI: shows the current task plus its next step, exposes time as secondary info, supports mark-done, and lets the user switch tasks without leaving Focus.

## Scope
- `/focus` route renders the active focus session (if any); without a session, shows a chooser
- **Active session UI**:
  - Large current task title + parent task chain (if subtask)
  - "Next step" sub-line — for parent tasks, this is the first open child task; for leaf tasks, it's `notes` truncated to one line
  - Soft time visibility: scheduled time shown small + grey ("9:00 – 9:30"); elapsed timer optional and toggleable; no countdown by default
  - Primary action: **Mark done** — closes the task, advances to next scheduled item if any
  - Secondary actions: **Switch task** (opens picker), **I'm stuck** (opens guided prompts — CL-STUCK-PROMPTS), **End focus** (returns to Home)
- **Focus session state** persisted to `focus_sessions` table (new migration `0007_focus_sessions.sql`) — id, user_id, task_id, started_at, ended_at NULL, source ('scheduled'|'ad-hoc')
- **Switch task picker**: list of today's remaining tasks (scheduled + backlog), select one → ends current session, starts new
- Without an active session: Focus screen shows "Start focus" button + list of today's items to pick from (also handles ad-hoc — see CL-FOCUS-ADHOC)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/Focus.tsx` (replace placeholder)

- `shared/src/model/focus.ts` — new file with FocusSession schema

## Acceptance
- Starting focus on a parent task with 2 open children renders title=parent, next-step=first child
- Mark done closes the active task (status='done') AND ends the focus session (`ended_at = now()`)
- Switch task ends current session, starts new one with a fresh started_at
- Reloading the app while a session is active resumes the same session
- Time display: scheduled time visible but small/grey; no countdown; toggle reveals elapsed timer
- E2E test: start focus, mark done, assert task status + session ended
